job.title: CPCD Analyst
job.description: About ASCAP The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) is a membership association of more than one million songwriters, composers and music publishers, and represents some of the world’s most talented music creators. Founded and governed by songwriters, composers and publishers, it is the only performing rights organization in the U.S. that operates on a not-for-profit basis. ASCAP licenses a repertory of over 20 million musical works to hundreds of thousands of businesses that use music, including streaming services, cable television, radio and satellite radio and brick and mortar businesses such as retail stores, hotels, clubs, restaurants and bars. ASCAP collects the licensing fees; identifies, matches and processes trillions of performances every year; and returns nearly 90 cents of every dollar back to its members as royalties. The ASCAP blanket license offers an efficient solution for businesses to legally perform ASCAP music while respecting the right of songwriters and composers to be paid fairly. ASCAP puts music creators first, advocating for their rights and the value of music on Capitol Hill, driving innovation that moves the industry forward, building community and providing the resources and support that creators need to succeed in their careers. Learn more and stay in touch at www.ascap.com , on X and Instagram @ASCAP and on Facebook . # # # Job Description: A Concert Program Analyst credits live concert performances by matching titles from concert programs for Symphonic, Recital, and Educational performances to works within the ASCAP Repertory. CPCD Analysts weigh performances based on their knowledge of the musical genre, instrumentation, and style before entering new title records into the database. Concert Program Analysts are also responsible for maintaining and updating work records with any newly received information. The ideal candidate for this role will be comfortable helping with any special projects that may be required, will possess strong communication skills, will be willing to assist other team members with workload, and will have the ability to identify and recommend process improvements. Areas of Responsibility & Accountability: Matching works on concert programs to titles within PREP (ASCAP’s internal database) Classifying works based on genre, instrumentation, and duration Utilizing various internet resources to create work records Merging duplicate works Researching programs submitted by members to include in ASCAP’s annual distribution Assisting any special projects on an as-needed basis Qualifications & Requirements: College degree in Music strongly preferred Ability to work independently Wide general knowledge of music, old and new (knowledge of classical and neo classical preferred, but not required) Familiarity with standard classical ensemble instrumentation and music forms Basic understanding of copyright protection and public domain concepts Critical thinking and research skills Knowledge of Google Workspace, Excel, Word, Adobe Acrobat This position requires the incumbent to be in the office one day per week Compensation/Benefits: Besides providing a unique and dynamic work environment, there are a few other reasons you should consider ASCAP in your career planning. We also offer generous benefit options that are comprehensive and provide the flexibility that most employees want and need. These health care and financial plan options include the following: A choice of either network-only provider medical and dental plans or more flexible medical and dental plans where you can see providers in or out-of-network Vision plan that offers both in and out-of-network provider options 401(k) Plan that offers pre-tax, Roth, and an after-tax employee contribution option which includes a company match An additional employer paid discretionary profit share contribution, regardless of your participation in the 401(k) Plan Generous time-off policy Health care and dependent care flexible spending accounts Short-term disability insurance/salary continuation and long-term disability insurance Company provided basic life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance Employee gym discounts at select gyms Commuter benefits Voluntary pet health insurance Voluntary auto and homeowner’s insurance Voluntary employee, spouse, and dependent life insurance options Voluntary ID protection Coverage The above summary of the current benefits is subject to the terms and conditions of the benefit plan documents. This summary is not complete and is subject to the terms of the underlying plan documents. Please note that ASCAP reserves the right to amend or otherwise revise or terminate, at any time and in its sole discretion, its benefit plans, programs, and policies. Occasional travel for in-person meetings may be required. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $50,000 to $50,000 and will be determined on an individualized basis depending on several factors that are unique to each candidate including geographic location (due to differences in the cost of labor), skills, education and prior relevant experience. Please be aware that ASCAP is not a nut-free or other allergen-free workplace. ASCAP is an equal opportunity employer. All ASCAP employment decisions are made on the basis of individual qualifications and performance and not on the basis of race, national origin, ethnicity, sex, age, marital status, sexual orientation or preference, gender identity, genetic information, disability, handicap, color, creed, religion, veteran status, or any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

job.title: Board Operator - WGAC-AM
job.description: Board Operator WGAC-AM | Augusta, GA Beasley Media Group is seeking reliable and detail-oriented Board Operators to join the team at WGAC-AM in Augusta, Georgia . The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, can multitask under pressure, and is committed to delivering a seamless listener experience. Board Operators work closely with the Program Director, on-air talent, and operations staff to ensure all programming, commercials, and broadcast elements air as scheduled. Key Responsibilities Execute seamless transitions between live, syndicated, and prerecorded programming. Monitor broadcast feeds and quickly troubleshoot technical issues as they arise. Ensure commercials, station imaging, and programming elements air accurately according to program logs. Maintain consistent on-air quality and programming flow. Collaborate with the Program Director and air talent to support daily broadcast operations. Edit audio content using Adobe Audition or similar audio editing software. Adhere to all FCC regulations and help protect the station’s FCC license. Qualifications Dependable with a strong work ethic and the ability to arrive at least 30 minutes prior to scheduled shifts for programming preparation. Previous experience operating a radio broadcast console and automation systems preferred; training will be provided for qualified candidates. Strong attention to detail and ability to follow commercial and programming logs accurately. Experience with audio editing software, preferably Adobe Audition. Ability to think quickly, make sound decisions, and perform effectively in high-pressure situations. Comfortable multitasking while maintaining accuracy and professionalism. Flexible schedule with availability to work early mornings, evenings, weekends, holidays, and other shifts as needed. Self-motivated team player capable of working independently. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside experienced broadcast professionals in a collaborative environment committed to excellence. Beasley Media Group, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Fluently translate progress, risk, and financial metrics between technical teams and corporate partners, ensuring information is fit-for-purpose for high-level stewardship and control. Collaborate with Program Director in preparing financial reporting for Governance. Communicate financial statuses and requirements effectively to diverse groups, including Corporate Finance, the Program Director, and Product Owners/Squad Leads. We are looking for a candidate with the following: 7 years relevant experience with 3 or more years managing project financials including agile/hybrid environments. Strong financial acumen, a deep understanding of financial mechanisms on projects and programs in the context of transformational and innovation projects. Able to understand actuals, and build short and long term forecasts in agile, traditional, and hybrid environments. Comfortable navigating ambiguity within an evolving program environment, bringing flexibility to financial forecasting as requirements and delivery details become more clearly defined over time. Understanding of different expenditure types in large transformative projects. Understanding of multiple funding models, from standard corporate budgets to loans paid via leases. Strong proficiency in utilizing data tools to track and report on financial performance metrics and turn complex information into tailored summaries. Experience building and using tools and reporting on financials in transformational/innovative initiatives. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, capable of interacting seamlessly with both highly technical and director-level governance. University degree in a relevant field or equivalent combination of training and experience. Functional bilingualism is an asset. Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing. You are passionate about providing breaking news to audiences, and injecting their mornings with some joy. You believe in collaborating with colleagues to make material resonate across CBC’s platforms. An understanding of Alberta’s political landscape, economic drivers and demographics, and a strong proven connection to the communities we serve in and around Edmonton and northern Alberta. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen. As part of this transformation, Innovation & Delivery is undertaking a large infrastructure project, with a goal to modernize our broadcasting capabilities. The Enterprise Applications Agile Practice team is supporting this program. This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines. Your Role: The Enterprise Applications Delivery - Agile Practice Team is looking for a Scrum Master with strong organizational and coaching skills and familiarity with Scaled Agile practices to lead squads in our audio and video editing tool replacement project known as Pyramid. This role can be based in our downtown Montreal or Toronto office. Reporting to the Director, Enterprise Application Delivery, you will guide and coach teams and support the transition to Agile in technical teams involved in this program. You will be responsible for ensuring the squads’ focus and effectiveness, partnering with Project teams and Project Managers to ensure priorities are known, and contribute to metrics and reporting. Leading by example, you will be an agent of change, introducing agile practices that will ensure focus, transparency and collaboration in your teams. You will also collaborate with other Scrum Masters to support Enterprise Applications in their Agile Transformation How will you make an impact? As Scrum Master, you will: Scaled Delivery & Squad Coaching Guide and coach multiple multidisciplinary Squads to implement Scaled Agile practices and principles to deliver high-quality digital/media products. Facilitate team-level events (Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Backlog Refinement, Sprint Reviews, and Retrospectives) ensuring continuous alignment with product vision and sprint goals. Maintain team focus, flow, and predictability while embedding rigorous quality standards (100% Definition of Done). Build a trusting, safe, and transparent environment focused on continuous improvement, autonomy, and open problem-solving. Scaled Alignment & Product Operating Model Integration Actively participate in program-level orchestration and scaled alignment events (such as PI Planning, Program Syncs, and Cross-Team Demos). Partner closely with Product Owners, Tech Leads, Architects, and Agile Delivery Leads to ensure backlog readiness, dependency mapping, and clear priority execution. Support the organizational transition from traditional project delivery to a product-led operating model, navigating hybrid environments smoothly when required. Identify, surface, and resolve daily impediments and cross-team dependencies, escalating systemic blockers through program governance when needed. Execution & Operationalization of the Product Transformation Approach Drive the successful implementation and adoption of the enterprise Product Operating Model by guiding teams through their core transformation steps: Transformation Intent: Align teams and stakeholders on shared business and operational outcomes. Ecosystem Diagnosis & Product Design: Identify flow bottlenecks, dependencies, and value stream friction points. MVP Operating Model Activation: Enable essential agile and product management practices across squads and governance layers. Gap Analysis & Prioritization: Assess current team maturity against target practices and prioritize capability gaps based on value and readiness. Roadmap Execution: Translate prioritized improvement areas into actionable, wave-based transformation increments. Continuous Adaptation: Track adoption metrics, measure progress, and continuously evolve team ways of working. Act as a proactive agent of change, breaking down operational silos and fostering a shared product culture across business and technology domains. Leverage delivery metrics, visual management boards, and transparent reporting to track agile maturity progression and team performance. Enablement & Peer Support across the Agile Practice Support, coach, and mentor other Scrum Masters across the enterprise practice, facilitating knowledge sharing, community alignment, and elevating overall scaled agile maturity. Collaborate within the Agile & Transformation practice to foster consistency in tooling, team working agreements, and scaled delivery standards. Contribute to the continuous refinement, evolution, and local enablement of the organization’s Agile Playbook and transformation practices. Perks you can look forward to: Four weeks of vacation per year. Work from home opportunities. Competitive total rewards package. Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology. Opportunities for continued learning and professional development - including access to e-learning services, customized courses and certification opportunities. A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity. Deep knowledge of agile practices, frameworks, and techniques, including Scaled Agile. Good knowledge of broadcast concepts and conversion projects are an asset. Among these key partners is the Transmission Engineering group, which is responsible for planning and implementing technical solutions to support the CBC/Radio-Canada broadcasting network (including, among others, traditional analog AM & FM radio, digital radio (HD Radio), digital television (ATSC) as well as C-Band and Ku-Band satellite distribution, and point-to-point links (STL)). Spectrum Engineering is a key area of expertise within Engineering Services . Composed of engineers acting as expert advisors in broadcasting and radio frequency (RF) management, the team's primary role is to provide the technical expertise, engineering documents, and essential advice required for the planning, protection, and maintenance of CBC/Radio-Canada's broadcasting and radiocommunication systems. Concretely, the group has several mandates, including to: Ensure the sustainability of our broadcasting infrastructure by managing and protecting the radio frequencies used by CBC/Radio-Canada. Perform engineering analyses to optimize the coverage of broadcasting stations and radiocommunication systems. Establish the official technical parameters of broadcasting stations (technical briefs). Ensure compliance with RF exposure limits at transmission sites located across the country (500+ sites) (Safety Code 6 - Health Canada). Perform specialized engineering studies and complex analyses applying the rigour and scientific approach of a professional engineer to meet the emerging needs of our internal partners and of new technologies. Job Opportunity CBC/Radio-Canada is currently looking to fill two permanent Spectrum Engineer positions, based in Toronto or Montreal. Perks you can look forward to: Four weeks vacation. Teleworking: hybrid mode with up to 3 days of teleworking per week. Good compensation package. Opportunities to work with various technologies. Language lessons. Opportunities for continuous learning and professional development. Creative and dynamic work environment where your ideas and contribution are listened to, valued and respected. Supportive leadership team committed to upholding the highest levels of diversity and inclusion. As a new Spectrum Engineer, you will be involved in a wide variety of projects: Complete coverage analyses to optimize the parameters (antenna, transmitter, transmission site, etc.) of radio (AM, FM, HD) and digital televisions stations (CRC-COVLAB). Write technical briefs (radio - television) according to the requirements of ISED's Broadcasting Rules and Procedures (BPR) (python programming). Submit applications to obtain broadcasting certificates and licenses from ISED (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) and CRTC (Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission). Develop programs or scripts to automate redundant tasks, implement new calculation methods, or speed up the production of engineering reports. Travel to different cities in Canada to perform signal measurements to assess our broadcasting services coverage (extent, intensity, quality). Perform RF exposure analyses (RNI, Safety Code 6 (SC6)) for the general public and workers for CBC/Radio-Canada transmission sites: Simulations of RF exposure levels. Perform RF measurements at transmission sites. Completed SC6 compliance reports. Make recommendations for transmission sites to remain compliant with Canadian safety standards. Perform point-to-point link analyses: Studio-Transmitter Link (Pathloss). Support satellite distribution systems. (C-Band & Ku-Band, LEO, 5G Broadcast, etc.) through analysis, evaluations, or licensing requests. Evaluate different technologies and write comprehensive technical reports (ATSC 3.0, HD radio, LEO, etc.). (required). Great interest in broadcasting. Five years of experience in broadcasting or telecommunications (asset). Individual should have the ability to undertake business affairs activities and lead or support negotiation for complex deals; distill complex contracts into manageable summaries; work with all units of ABC News in servicing internal and external production work and internal on-air and off-air talent deals; and work within tight deadlines on multiple projects in a fast-paced environment. Familiarity with documentary, docu-follow, and narrative non-fiction projects is also needed. Responsibilities: Negotiate independently or assist in the negotiation of a high volume of deals in a fast-paced environment in connection with developing, producing, and/or acquiring content for a wide variety of programming, including non-scripted series, limited series, documentaries, and/or specials. Negotiate ancillary production related agreements such as producer agreements, talent agreements, option agreements, and underlying rights agreements. Negotiate contracts for ABC News on-air and off-air talent. Such negotiation incorporates determining major deal points including compensation and production duties. Takes assigned tasks and accomplishes them by creating work plans and procedures in partnership with key stake holders. Enforces applicable policies and may recommend changes in areas where potential improvement can be cultivated. Effectively uses available resources to meet operating plans. Partners with various internal teams including, but not limited to, legal, production, labor, standards, publicity, editorial/creative and marketing to ensure that all deals adhere to company policy, deadlines are met and shares information to transact business agreements and improve cross-departmental processes. Supports deals after close by tracking pertinent dates and cash flow models. Reviewing and approving invoices and payments in conjunction with production management. Manage relationships with agents, lawyers and executives throughout entertainment industry. Basic Qualifications: At least seven (7) years’ experience in media, business, or corporate law. Must have strong familiarity with documentary, narrative non-fiction world. Must have outstanding writing, reviewing, negotiating of contracts. Must have excellent communication and organization skills. Must be superior at building and maintaining internal and external relationships. Must be highly organized. Preferred Qualifications: At least three (3) years’ experience in project or processes management. J.D. degree from an ABA-accredited law school and admission to a state bar. Required Education: Bachelor’s degree The hiring range for this position in New York, NY is $110,100 to $147,600 per year. The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered.

job.title: Senior Product Manager II, Content & Media Platform
job.description: Technology is at the heart of Disney’s past, present, and future. Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology is a global organization of engineers, product developers, designers, technologists, data scientists, and more – all working to build and advance the technological backbone for Disney’s media business globally. The team marries technology with creativity to build world-class products, enhance storytelling, and drive velocity, innovation, and scalability for our businesses. We are Storytellers and Innovators. Creators and Builders. Entertainers and Engineers. We work with every part of The Walt Disney Company’s media portfolio to advance the technological foundation and consumer media touch points serving millions of people around the world. Here are a few reasons why we think you’d love working here: Building the future of Disney’s media: Our Technologists are designing and building the products and platforms that will power our media, advertising, and distribution businesses for years to come. Reach, Scale & Impact: More than ever, Disney’s technology and products serve as a signature doorway for fans' connections with the company’s brands and stories. Disney+. Hulu. ESPN. ABC. ABC News…and many more. These products and brands – and the unmatched stories, storytellers, and events they carry – matter to millions of people globally. Innovation: We develop and implement groundbreaking products and techniques that shape industry norms, and solve complex and distinctive technical problems. Product Management is responsible for driving the overall user experience, feature strategies and concepts, and engagement paradigms for Disney Entertainment & ESPN's global portfolio of consumer-facing streaming and digital products – including Disney+, Hulu, ESPN, ABC, ABC News, Nat Geo, Marvel, and Star Wars. About the Role At The Walt Disney Company, we believe in the power of storytelling to inform, connect, and inspire. We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager II to lead the evolution of the Media Platform within the ABC News CMS, which powers content creation and publishing to ABC News websites, mobile apps, and digital platforms. In this role, you will own the media platform end-to-end - including asset models, ingestion pipelines, AI integrations and metadata systems - and shape how editors create, manage and publish media within the CMS, ensuring workflows are intuitive, scalable, and tightly integrated across authoring and downstream experiences. This role is ideal for a product leader who thrives in complex, technical environments and brings strong product judgment to ambiguous problems - translating cross-system complexity into clear, scalable solutions and driving alignment across teams to deliver consistent, high-quality outcomes. Responsibilities Strategy & Vision Define and drive a clear product strategy for media capabilities within the ABC News CMS that support digital publishing across web and mobile experiences. Establish success metrics that reflect editorial efficiency, system performance and reliability. Own the long-term strategy for ABC News media platform evolution, including integration of future capabilities such as video authoring, platform consolidation and AI workflow optimizations. Set cross-domain strategy for media capabilities, ensuring alignment across authoring, media, and curation workflows. Media Platform Leadership Define the media object model - structure, metadata, and lifecycle - for video and image assets used in digital publishing. Own the experience of media workflows within the ABC News CMS, including how editors upload, manage, and edit media metadata, ensuring workflows are intuitive, efficient, and aligned to editorial needs. Drive convergence of fragmented workflows into a unified, platform-driven approach. Cross-Functional Collaboration Deliver end-to-end media capabilities in partnership with engineering, design, and editorial teams. Drive integration of media workflows across authoring and curation domains in partnership with product leads. Build alignment across stakeholders, ensuring shared understanding of goals, priorities, and outcomes. Execution & Delivery Translate strategy into actionable roadmaps and deliver in iterative, measurable phases. Lead complex, cross-system initiatives such as media migration and workflow consolidation. Launch products with strong coordination, clear communication, and a focus on impact. Audience-Centered Product Development Reduce friction in editorial workflows, enabling users to spend more time focused on journalism and less on technical processes. Partner closely with design and authoring product leads to improve the CMS experience for publishing and managing media, including metadata editing and asset management workflows. Balance editorial needs with technical feasibility and long-term platform scalability. Stakeholder Leadership Build strong, trusted relationships across product, engineering, editorial, and business teams. Communicate product strategy, progress, and tradeoffs clearly to senior leadership. Act as a platform leader, ensuring the broader ecosystem evolves in a cohesive and scalable way. Qualifications Minimum Qualifications 7+ years of product management experience, ideally in content platforms or media technology. Experience building and scaling platform products, such as content management systems, asset management systems, or enterprise products. Proven ability to define product vision and align cross-functional teams, including engineering, design, and editorial stakeholders. Experience delivering complex products with measurable impact on performance, scalability, or workflow efficiency. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with comfort using both qualitative insights and quantitative data. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate ideas to diverse audiences. Technical fluency and experience working closely with engineering teams in agile environments. Experience navigating ambiguity and making high-impact tradeoffs across multiple product domains. A user-focused mindset with a passion for enabling high-quality content creation and publishing experiences. Bachelor’s degree required #DISNEYTECH The hiring range for this position in New York City, NY is $163,100 - $218,700 per year and in Glendale, CA is $155,700 - $208,700 per year. The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered.

job.title: VP, Operations & Business Planning (Finance)
job.description: The Vice President, Operations & Business Planning serves as the senior finance leader for WPVI and WTVD, providing strategic financial leadership across both stations. This executive is responsible for financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, long-range and capital planning, investment analysis, business performance management, and strategic decision support. As a key member of the executive leadership teams, the VP serves as a trusted advisor to the Presidents & General Managers and OTV leadership, translating financial and operational insights into strategies that drive performance, growth, profitability, and effective resource allocation. This position plays a critical role in shaping the long-term direction of the business through strategic financial leadership, operational discipline, investment evaluation, workforce planning, and enterprise-wide decision-making. Based in Philadelphia, this role requires regular travel to Raleigh-Durham, including approximately monthly visits and additional travel as business needs require. Key Responsibilities: Serve as a member of the executive leadership teams for WPVI and WTVD, providing strategic financial and business leadership. Partner with Presidents & General Managers and OTV leadership to evaluate business performance, strategy, investments, resource allocation, and growth opportunities. Lead financial strategies that support short-term performance objectives and long-term growth initiatives. Evaluate operational and market opportunities that improve profitability, efficiency, and long-term business sustainability. Direct budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, capital planning, and performance management activities across the two-station portfolio. Lead Annual Operating Plans (AOP), Latest Operating Plans (LOP), forecasts, budgets, and long-range strategic planning. Develop financial models, scenario analyses, and investment analyses to support key business initiatives and investment decisions. Develop recommendations regarding capital investments, resource allocation, and business growth opportunities. Align financial resources with enterprise priorities and station objectives. Advise leadership on organizational design, workforce planning, resource allocation, and operational investments. Monitor financial performance and key business drivers across both stations. Translate complex financial and operational data into actionable insights and recommendations for executive leadership. Lead regular business reviews, performance discussions, and strategic planning sessions with senior stakeholders. Identify financial risks and opportunities and develop strategies to improve business outcomes. Create executive-level reporting and insights to support informed decision-making. Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing finance organization, fostering accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and operational excellence. Build organizational capability through talent development, succession planning, and mentoring. Partner with OTV, Corporate Finance, Human Resources, Legal, and operational leaders on strategic initiatives and business priorities. Support technology investments, capital planning initiatives, and major business transformation efforts. Ensure compliance with company policies, financial controls, and reporting requirements. Maintain the integrity of financial processes and promote strong financial stewardship across the organization. Required Qualifications: 12+ years of progressive experience in finance, FP&A, accounting, corporate finance, strategic finance, or business planning. Significant leadership experience managing finance teams and partnering with executive leadership. Demonstrated expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, long-range planning, and financial strategy development. Proven ability to influence executive decision-making through data-driven insights and recommendations. Strong financial modeling, analytical, communication, and executive presentation skills. Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and managing competing business priorities. Ability and willingness to travel regularly to Raleigh-Durham, including approximately monthly visits and additional travel as needed. Preferred Qualifications: MBA, CPA, or equivalent advanced finance credential. Experience in media, broadcasting, entertainment, digital media, or other consumer-facing businesses. Experience leading finance functions within a complex, matrixed organization. Experience supporting multi-site, regional, or portfolio-based business operations. Systems Knowledge: SAP Cognos Coupa WideOrbit Advanced Microsoft Excel Microsoft Office Suite Required Education: Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field. The hiring range for this position in Philadelphia, PA is $176,700.00 to $236,900.00 per year. The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered.

job.title: Associate Video Producer, Social - PEOPLE
job.description: Job Title Associate Video Producer, Social - PEOPLE Job Description I. Job Summary | Major goals and objectives. The Associate Video Producer edits and occasionally shoots videos for PEOPLE’s social media and app, with an emphasis on “verticalizing” longform video features and creating social teasers/trailers for bombshell, exclusive interviews. Their mission is to ensure that PEOPLE’s social and app video content is visually arresting and narratively compelling. This person should have passion for shortform storytelling, an expertise in video producing and editing, and a desire to entice people to watch and engage with content. They must know how to hook and hold busy users’ attention. The ideal candidate knows how to make videos go viral on TikTok and Reels. They must be comfortable producing celebrity talent. The Associate Video Producer will report to the Senior Video Producer. They will work closely with the PEOPLE Video team to edit exclusive video interviews and concepts for social and the PEOPLE app, turning raw footage into social gold. They will also work closely with a team of motion graphics designers to develop and execute visuals for social series and tentpoles. This role will require industry experience and the ability to join meetings and assist with guidance of other team members. They must be able to balance different projects based on business priorities and the news cycle, delivering high-quality videos on deadline. II. Essential Job Functions Weight % | Accountabilities, Actions and Expected Measurable Results 70% - Produce and edit videos for social and the PEOPLE app 20% - Work closely with reporters, editors, content creators, designers and the Video team 10% - Attend events on behalf of brand and capture content, and other duties as assigned III. job.description: Job Title Commercial Counsel Job Description About The Position: The Commercial Counsel is a key member of People Inc's Legal team, serving as a trusted legal advisor to the business and leading the review, negotiation, and implementation of the company's commercial contracting processes. In-office Expectations - NYC Location: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely up to two days per week. Demonstrated interest in intellectual property transactions, privacy, AI, product counseling, or data licensing. job.title: Director, Data Science
job.description: Job Title Director, Data Science Job Description About The Position | Major Goals and Objectives and Location Requirements: People Inc. is America’s largest print and digital publisher, reaching tens of millions of readers every day. We’re hiring a Director of Data Science to lead customer intelligence and personalization for our entertainment brands, helping shape products and experiences that inform, engage, and inspire our audiences. In this role, you’ll build a deeper understanding of our customers across product engagement, marketing response, and lifecycle behavior. You’ll partner closely with Product, Marketing, and Editorial teams to turn data into actionable insights that drive growth, while working with Data Operations and Engineering to ensure our models, measurement systems, and insights can scale effectively. You’ll apply statistical modeling and machine learning to product and marketing challenges across customer segmentation, acquisition, engagement, retention, and lifetime value, with a particular focus on mobile app experiences. You’ll own models and analyses that support personalization, automated marketing, attribution, experimentation, and lifecycle optimization across apps, newsletters, and other customer touchpoints, translating complex audience behavior into clear recommendations and measurable business impact. Schedule Requirements: In-office Expectations: This position is fully remote with no in-office requirements, (might require coming into an office periodically for team meetings, etc.) About The Team | The Team and/or Brand: People Inc. is the largest premium publisher in the world. Every day, tens of millions of people come to us for help and inspiration. Our library of hundreds of thousands of articles helps our users understand how to deal with day-to-day challenges. You will work with a team of data scientists, collaborating with cross-functional groups to leverage this incredible dataset to understand both our content and our users' needs. This knowledge will be used to identify and build out new products that leverage the behavioral information within our extensive data. About The Position’s Contributions: Weight % Accountabilities, Actions, and Expected Measurable Results Lead and grow a data science team to develop predictive models that estimate customer lifetime value using advanced statistical and machine learning techniques. Analyze and understand customer interactions across app, web, social media, and email touchpoints to identify and optimize engagement opportunities. Own product funnel and engagement analysis, including onboarding completion, feature adoption, feature stickiness, and session behavior, as distinct from marketing-funnel metrics such as acquisition and retention. Leverage data-driven insights to build customer segmentation models, identifying high-value users and informing content and product recommendations. Partner with Product and Editorial teams to translate user understanding into differentiated experiences across the app, newsletters, and other customer interactions, feeding insights directly into the product development cycle. This includes the sizing of opportunities and assessment of product success. Design online A/B testing experiments to measure the impact of product changes, personalization, and full-funnel marketing interventions. Ensure effective collaboration between data science teams and other departments. Advocate for resources and tools to advance data capabilities. Align data initiatives with company objectives. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements: Education: PhD or advanced degree in Data Science, Economics, Business Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics, or similar quantitative field, or equivalent experience. Experience: 7+ years of experience in data science and machine learning with a strong focus in the area of customer behavior, product analytics, and marketing-focused problems. 5+ years of experience leading a team of data scientists. Ability to lead product and funnel analytics on web and mobile platforms with a focus on providing actionable insights, not just data outputs. Solid foundation in causal inference, survival analysis, and time series analysis, especially as applied to marketing and customer behavior. Strong proficiency in Python and SQL for data analysis and model development. Familiarity with Claude Code/Codex and how they can be used reliably (and where they fail) in a data science workflow. Strong strategic and operational capabilities. Excellent leadership and communication skills. Ability to communicate complex analyses clearly to non-technical marketing and business stakeholders. Drives adoption of new data science methods and technologies to continually expand what the product can do. Specific Knowledge, Skills, Certifications and Abilities: Experience with large-scale search and recommendation systems in media, e-commerce, or advertising space. Experience working with large-scale analytics platforms (e.g., BigQuery). Exposure to reinforcement learning or bandit approaches for personalization or offer optimization. Advanced experimentation techniques, including multivariate testing, factorial designs, and CUPED. Experience with Bayesian statistical methods for inference and decision-making under uncertainty. Experience with forecasting models and advanced lifecycle or retention modeling. Applied NLP experience for content classification, semantic search, or audience understanding. Track record of leading end-to-end data science projects from problem framing through deployment and impact measurement. Confidence and pride in representing Data Science as a strategic partner to Marketing and other business teams. % Travel Required ( Approximate ): ~5%, ability to travel periodically/quarterly for team meetings/events preferred but flexible based on candidate needs It is the policy of People Inc. to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. job.description: Job Title Director, Executive Compensation Job Description The Director, Executive Compensation serves as the leader and subject matter expert for the company’s equity and executive compensation programs. This hands-on role is responsible for administering and optimizing the equity compensation program at People Incorporated and ensuring a seamless experience for all participants. Reporting to the VP of Total Rewards, this role interacts with Finance, Legal, and HR. The ideal candidate will balance technical excellence in equity governance with the executive presence required to design, communicate, and execute competitive reward strategies across the company. The position is based in the New York City corporate headquarters and is hybrid in-office with the ability to work remotely up to 2 days per week. Equity Program Administration Manage and process the full lifecycle of global equity awards: grant setup, vesting, releases, cancellations, terminations/retirement, and quarterly dividends across multiple jurisdictions and equity structures. Manage and optimize the employee equity database. Maintain flawless data integrity, update employee records, and generate routine and ad-hoc reports. Act as a trusted, accessible stock plan expert to all levels of the organization, including executives and board members, providing support and addressing inquiries with clarity, accuracy, and timeliness. Coordinate with Payroll and Finance regarding equity vests and reporting. Provide guidance to HRBPs and Subsidiary companies as needed. Review, interpret, and optimize stock plan data. Track and report on critical equity metrics including share utilization, burn rate, overhang, and dilution to inform long-term budgeting and forecasting. Prepare projections and provide recommendations on budgets. Exercise sound judgment to resolve complex stock plan participant matters and address evolving stock plan provisions, balancing business needs and employee experience considerations. Proactively educate employees on their equity plans and grants. Prepare and review stock plan participant communications, statements, and educational materials, ensuring clarity and comprehension across diverse participant groups. Own the strategic relationship and service level agreements (SLAs) with external stock plan administrators (e.g., Morgan Stanley), ensuring seamless platform optimization and flawless database data integrity. Act as the technical advisor on the equity and compensation implications of corporate restructurings, subsidiary management, and Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A). Oversee equity plan compliance, monitoring insider trading policies, managing pre-clearance lists, and enforcing corporate blackout periods in partnership with Legal. Executive Compensation, Proxy & Governance Partner directly with the VP of Total Rewards to strategize, draft, and deliver high-impact, Board-level materials and data visualizations for the quarterly Compensation Committee meetings. Contribute to executive compensation-related regulatory filings and disclosures, including the Compensation Discussion & Analysis (CD&A) and related proxy statement content. Monitor and interpret evolving investor expectations and proxy advisor perspectives, regulatory developments, firm strategy and market practices and translate these into practical implications for Total Rewards program design and disclosure. Lead executive benchmarking, peer group selection, and competitive pay analysis for senior leadership. Ensure regulatory compliance for Section 16 executive and Board members and assist in the preparation of SEC Form filings . General Compensation & Projects Serve as a trusted advisor to senior management by providing strategic guidance and execution support for Total Rewards programs, especially compensation programs impacting senior leadership. Serve as a trusted partner to HR and Finance with Compensation initiatives throughout the year. Support the Compensation team by collaborating on Compensation philosophy and with the year-end compensation cycle. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements: Education: Bachelor’s degree in HR, Finance, or Business. CCP certification is a plus. Experience: 8+ years of progressive experience in compensation in a publicly traded, mid-to-large-sized company with specific experience in hands-on equity administration including stock options, restricted stock, and performance-based stock awards. Specific Knowledge, Skills, Certifications and Abilities: Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and quantitative skills with a focus on detail and data accuracy. Advanced Sheets/Excel Capabilities: Mastery of advanced spreadsheet functions (lookups, index/match, pivot tables, complex data modeling) to manipulate and interpret large datasets. Discretion & Judgment: A proven problem-solving mindset with the ability to think critically, exercise good judgment, and handle highly confidential executive data with total discretion. Agility & Time Management: Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, managing multiple competing priorities and tight deadlines seamlessly. Communication: Exceptional communication skills with the ability to articulate complex equity and compensation topics clearly to both entry-level employees and executives. Autonomy: A proactive, self-starter mentality who takes initiative and works independently while remaining a highly collaborative team player. job.description: Job Title Editorial Director, Hot Luck Job Description About The Position | Major goals and objectives and location requirements Hot Luck is seeking an Editorial Director to lead the editorial vision, content strategy, audience development, and multi-platform growth of one of the most distinctive food and music festival brands in the country. Reporting to Food & Wine and Hot Luck Editor in Chief Hunter Lewis, this role will oversee the development and execution of a year-round content ecosystem that celebrates the people, culture, food, music, hospitality, and experiences that define the Hot Luck brand. The Editorial Director will be responsible for expanding Hot Luck beyond its annual festival footprint and building a best-in-class content operation across digital, video, audio, social, newsletters, live events, and branded content. This includes launching and scaling a Hot Luck YouTube channel, developing recurring social video franchises, producing editorially-driven sponsorship programs, growing a robust newsletter portfolio, and helping establish a Hot Luck radio and audio presence that extends the brand's reach and influence throughout the year. The ideal candidate is an entrepreneurial editorial leader with experience building modern media brands across platforms. They are equally comfortable developing long-range content strategies, launching new editorial products, managing teams and contributors, and creating compelling stories that resonate across digital, social, video, audio, and live experiences. This position may be based in either New York City or Austin, Texas. Candidates should be comfortable working closely with teams in both markets and traveling regularly to Austin throughout the year, with increased travel during festival planning and execution periods. job.description: Job Title Executive Assistant, Corporate Governance & Board Operations Job Description About The Position: The Executive Assistant, Corporate Governance & Board Operations provides high-level administrative and governance support to the Deputy General Counsel and legal leadership team, focusing on board management and corporate governance. As the central liaison for the Board of Directors, this role ensures seamless communication and meticulous preparation of materials for executive meetings. The ideal candidate is a proactive, highly organized professional who handles competing demands with exceptional judgment, strict confidentiality, and high integrity. Hybrid 3x a week- NYC In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week. About The Team: The People Inc. legal team operates as a trusted strategic partner across the enterprise, safeguarding the company’s assets, reputation, and compliance standards. We are a collaborative, detail-oriented, and high-performing team that values integrity, proactive problem-solving, and continuous improvement. This role interacts closely with executive leadership, the Board of Directors, and external stakeholders, representing the legal department with professionalism and poise. About The Position’s Contributions: 75% Board of Directors & Corporate Governance Support: Manage logistics for Board and Committee meetings, including scheduling, facilities, and virtual arrangements. Prepare and distribute confidential Board materials, agendas, and presentations per established timelines. Maintain the Board portal to ensure secure and timely document updates. Coordinate the collection of reports and presentations from executive leadership for Board books. Track Board action items, resolutions, and follow-up requests to ensure timely completion. Maintain official corporate records, including minutes, resolutions, and governance documentation. Assist with governance initiatives, such as calendars, director onboarding, and shareholder meetings. Oversee the execution and retention of resolutions, written consents, and executive certifications. 10% Operational Excellence: Identify opportunities to improve administrative and operational processes that increase efficiency within the Legal department. Build collaborative relationships across Legal, Human Resources, Finance, Executive Leadership, and other business functions. Anticipate business needs and proactively recommend solutions that enhance executive effectiveness and department operations. 10% Executive Admin Support to Deputy General Counsel , Head of Corporate Legal Affairs & Litigation : Provide comprehensive executive support to the Deputy General Counsel (calendar, travel, expenses, and communications) Facilitate legal operations (meeting coordination, document management, contract administration, budgeting, and vendor support). 5% Executive and Legal Team Support Back-Up: Serve as back-up coverage during the Executive Legal Assistant's absence to provide comprehensive executive support to the SVP and General Counsel as needed including: calendar, travel, expenses, and communications, meeting coordination, document management, contract administration, budgeting, and vendor support. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements: Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Legal Studies, or a related field preferred; or equivalent combination of education and professional experience. job.title: GSOC Coordinator
job.description: Job Title GSOC Coordinator Job Description About The Position | Major Goals and Objectives and Location Requirements: People Inc. is seeking an experienced GSOC Coordinator to serve as a trusted operational resource within the Global Security Operations Center. This position performs the full range of GSOC operator duties while also supporting advanced enterprise security work involving intelligence, investigations, travel security, executive protection, and crisis management. Reporting to the Manager, GSOC & Intelligence, the Coordinator operates security systems, manages incidents and communications, conducts research and assessments, and supports sensitive security matters requiring sound judgment, discretion, strong writing, and independent decision-making. Schedule Requirements: Full In-Office In-office Expectations: This position is a fully in-office role due to the nature of the work being done. About The Team | The Team and/or Brand: The Security team at People Inc. is responsible for ensuring the safety and security of employees, facilities, and assets across all office site locations. The team partners closely with contracted security staff, reception, facilities, event teams, and law enforcement agencies to deliver a consistent and resilient security program. About The Position’s Contributions: GSOC and Site Security Operations Operate the GSOC and continuously monitor alarms, CCTV, access control, life-safety systems, and other enterprise security technologies. Receive, assess, document, and coordinate the response to security incidents, emergencies, system alerts, and requests for assistance. Dispatch security personnel, maintain communications with field operations, and ensure timely escalation to Security Management and appropriate business partners. Prepare and distribute mass notifications, emergency communications, incident updates, and other enterprise security messages when authorized. Support access-control administration, video review, incident documentation, daily logs, shift turnover, and security-system troubleshooting. Intelligence and Investigative Support Conduct open-source intelligence research, social media monitoring, threat-actor research, and other authorized intelligence collection in support of active security matters. Assist with threat assessments, workplace violence concerns, criminal and administrative investigations, background research, and investigative case support. Support executive and brand threat monitoring by identifying, documenting, and escalating information that may indicate risk to employees, executives, offices, events, or company operations. Produce clear, accurate, and timely incident reports, intelligence summaries, investigative memoranda, and executive-ready briefing materials. Travel, Executive, and Crisis Support Monitor employee and executive travel, assess destination and geopolitical risk, and support traveler accountability during incidents or emergencies. Provide operational and intelligence support for executive travel, protective operations, corporate events, and other elevated-risk activities. Monitor global incidents, severe weather, civil unrest, geopolitical developments, and other events that could affect company personnel or operations. Support crisis activations through situational awareness, communications, incident tracking, escalation, and preparation of situation reports. Program and Operational Support Work closely with Security Operations personnel to coordinate field response, information sharing, and operational support during incidents and special events. Support the Manager, GSOC & Intelligence with program documentation, procedures, audits, metrics, training materials, and special projects. Handle sensitive company, employee, investigative, and executive information with discretion and in accordance with established protocols. Maintain a professional, service-oriented approach when assisting employees, executives, visitors, law enforcement, vendors, and business partners. Demonstrated experience with investigations, intelligence research, threat assessments, analytical research, or other complex security work beyond routine monitoring and dispatch. Ability to independently operate a command center environment, manage competing priorities, assess incomplete information, and make timely, defensible decisions. Excellent written communication and report-writing skills, including the ability to organize complex information into concise operational or executive summaries. Strong judgment, discretion, attention to detail, and ability to handle sensitive or confidential information. Working knowledge of CCTV, access control, alarm monitoring, incident management, mass notification, and common GSOC or physical security technologies. Strong computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office and the ability to learn investigative, intelligence, travel-monitoring, and security-system platforms. Ability to successfully complete required pre-employment screening and obtain required certifications after hire. Experience in a GSOC, Security Operations Center, Emergency Operations Center, Fusion Center, intelligence unit, investigative unit, or comparable environment. job.description: Job Title GTM Manager, Ad Product Commercialization Job Description About The Position : The GTM Manager, Ad Product Commercialization is a mid-to-senior execution leader responsible for the day-to-day coordination, commercial readiness, and field adoption of our enterprise ad product portfolio. Based in our New York City office, this role serves as the critical, high-touch bridge between our product capabilities and sales execution. As the ultimate "keeper of the Ad Product Catalog," you will ensure that our New York-based revenue teams—including Sellers, Account Strategists, and Brand Marketers—fully understand our ad products, their operational nuances, and how to position them for maximum yield. Additionally, you will act as the on-the-ground project manager ushering new products through the formal GTM process, ensuring cross-functional alignment and gathering real-time field feedback to optimize our commercial engine. Hybrid 3x a week- NYC In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week. About The Team: The Ad Product Commercialization team partners across Product, Sales, Brand Marketing, Revenue Operations, Ad Operations, and Commercial organizations to successfully bring advertising products to market. The team enables revenue growth by ensuring product launches are well coordinated, sales teams are equipped for success, and customer feedback continuously informs product evolution. About The Position’s Contributions: 35% Ad Product Catalog Governance & Advisory Single Source of Truth: Own and maintain the comprehensive Ad Product Catalog. Ensure all product specifications, packaging rules, pricing guidelines, and operational constraints are meticulously updated, accurate, and accessible. Provide rapid, clear answers to complex, nuanced questions regarding ad product capabilities and custom configuration rules. Coordinate timelines, keep cross-functional stakeholders on schedule, and prevent rollout bottlenecks. Operational Readiness & Briefings: Translate dense, technical ad product mechanics into clear, digestible operational instructions. Lead internal briefings and training sessions for revenue teams detailing what a product is, who it is for, and how to book it. 30% Field Adoption & Commercial Yield Analysis Data-Driven Optimization: Regularly analyze internal sales data and product adoption metrics. Identify which packages are driving the highest yield and surface trends regarding what is selling well versus what isn't. On-the-Ground Feedback Loops: Leverage your physical presence in the NYC office to build deep trust with sellers and CROs. Proactively capture field feedback, understand seller pain points, and investigate the "why" behind product adoption data to inform future iterations. job.title: Senior Data Scientist
job.description: Job Title Senior Data Scientist Job Description About The Position | As a Senior Data Scientist for personalization, you will own the science behind the recommendation engine that powers each user’s personalized product feed. Starting from our user-saved product signals and a live catalog ingested from thousands of retailer feeds, you will design, build, evaluate, and continuously improve the models that learn each user’s taste across brand, category, color, price point, and fit. This is a hands-on, full-cycle role. You will take a recommendation problem from raw data all the way to a production model running on our existing MLOps stack — you own the model layer, not the infrastructure. Our platform team already operates the feature store, serving, and autoscaling; your job is to decide what to model, prove it works through rigorous offline and online experimentation, ship it, and iterate as behavioral signals accumulate. A defining challenge of this role is cold-start. We are launching with a small behavioral dataset and a catalog scaling from hundreds of thousands of products toward tens of millions. You will need strong commerce and product-data intuition to produce high-quality recommendations before rich click data exists — and the experimental discipline to keep improving them as it arrives. This is a foundational hire that will shape how millions of users discover products they love. Remote or Hybrid 3x a week NYC In-office Expectations: This position offers remote work flexibility; however, if you reside within a commutable distance our offices in New York, the expectation is to work from the office three days per week. About The Team: | _______________________________________________________________________________ Our next-generation product discovery platform connects shoppers with the things they love across thousands of retail partners. Users save, organize, and share products they're excited about — and our platform turns those signals into a deeply personalized shopping experience. We ingest live product feeds from thousands of retailers and use a rich understanding of each user's taste to surface the right product at the right moment. We're building the recommendation engine at the heart of this shopping experience — a system that understands not just what people save, but why they save it. This is a foundational hire that will shape how millions of users discover products they love. About The Positions Contributions: 35% Recommendation & Personalization Modeling Own the design and development of the core recommendation models that turn user-saved product data into a personalized feed. Develop multi-signal models spanning brand affinity, category, color/visual attributes, fit and sizing, price sensitivity, and trend. Select and justify approaches across collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, content-based, and hybrid/neural methods (e.g., two-tower and other embedding models), and know when each applies. Build product and user embeddings that capture semantic similarity across the catalog and power candidate generation and retrieval. Design cold-start strategies that produce high-quality recommendations for new users and newly ingested products with little or no behavioral history. 25% Experimentation & Measurement Define what “good” personalization means and how it is measured. Establish rigorous offline evaluation (ranking and relevance metrics, sound holdout design) and connect it to online outcomes. Design, run, and read out A/B and multivariate experiments, and translate results into clear product and business decisions. Bring statistical discipline — sound experiment design, awareness of bias and confounding, and honest interpretation — so the team can trust which changes actually move engagement. 20% Data, Signals & Feature Understanding Develop deep intuition for Picksy’s product catalog and user signals. Turn implicit behavior (saves, clicks, dwell, shares) and catalog attributes into meaningful model features, writing SQL against BigQuery to pull, join, and shape raw data into training/evaluation datasets. Apply NLP and computer-vision techniques — including modern embedding and LLM-based approaches — to extract structured attributes (category, color, material, fit) from unstructured product descriptions and imagery, and to enrich sparse catalog data. Partner with data engineering on data quality, freshness, and coverage as the catalog scales from hundreds of thousands toward tens of millions of products. 20% Full-Cycle Ownership & Productionization Take models from prototype to production yourself. Write clean, production-quality code and deploy into the existing MLOps pipeline (feature store, training, serving, monitoring) rather than building infrastructure from scratch. Own model performance in production: instrument it, watch for drift and degradation, and iterate as behavioral signals accumulate. Document models, features, and decisions clearly, and collaborate closely with the MLOps, engineering, and product teams to integrate the model layer into the live product. Education: Master's degree or higher in Computer Science, Statistics, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field; or equivalent practical experience. Experience: You combine the modeling depth of an applied/data scientist with the pragmatism to ship end-to-end. You bring: Strong data science fundamentals: statistics, experimental design, and evaluation methodology, with the analytical ability to turn model results into clear product and business decisions. Demonstrated ownership of the full A/B testing lifecycle: designing experiments, running them, reading them out, and deciding; not just reporting offline metrics. Experience designing, training, and deploying embedding models and vector retrieval (e.g., Milvus, Pinecone, or Vertex AI Vector Search) for product or content similarity at catalog scale. Direct experience with cold-start / sparse-signal personalization: building useful recommendations from a new catalog, new users, or both. This is a core, day-one challenge of the role. Strong Python and modern ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX) plus the standard scientific stack (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn). You write production-quality code, not just notebooks. Strong SQL: hands-on experience querying large datasets in a cloud data warehouse (BigQuery preferred) to pull, join, and assemble the training and evaluation datasets that feed your models. This is a daily part of the role. Experience deploying and serving models on a cloud ML platform: GCP Vertex AI strongly preferred (SageMaker or equivalent acceptable) and you are comfortable owning the full model lifecycle: training, deployment, versioning, and monitoring. Commerce intuition: you’ve worked with product catalogs and understand merchandising, category, and PM concerns. It shows up in how you talk about catalogs and taste, not just models. Curiosity and pragmatism about emerging AI, particularly LLMs and modern retrieval/ranking, with a track record of bringing new techniques into real production use. Strong written and verbal communication; able to explain technical tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Nice to have: Applied NLP and/or computer vision for extracting structured attributes from product text and imagery. Experience with adaptive recommendation and experimentation methods; multi-armed or contextual bandits. Public writing or conference talks on recommendation, personalization, or ranking work. Early-stage or commerce experience where you wore multiple hats and shipped against real business metrics (e.g., commerce SaaS or a vertical commerce startup). job.description: Job Title Senior Marketing Manager, Style Job Description I. Job Summary: About the Position | Major goals and objectives and location requirements People Inc. is seeking a Senior Marketing Manager to join the Beauty & Style vertical, contributing to the growth of brands including InStyle, Byrdie, PEOPLE, Entertainment Weekly, and more. job.title: Senior Product Manager, Privacy & Trust
job.description: Job Title Senior Product Manager, Privacy & Trust Job Description About The Position | Major goals and objectives and location requirements We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to take charge of our data privacy and platform strategy. You will be the point person for balancing our business needs, like audience growth and personalization, with the reality of global privacy regulations. This role is a mix of high-level roadmap planning and deep-in-the-weeds technical problem solving, specifically regarding our Data Subject Request (DSR) platform. Hybrid 3x a week- (New York, NY) In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week. About The Team: At People Inc., we treat reader trust as our most valuable asset. This role is not just building a platform; this role is building the infrastructure that allows our readers to trust us with their data. This team solves hard, "real-world" technical problems that have a tangible impact. About The Positions Contributions: Weight % | Accountabilities, Actions and Expected Measurable Results 20% | Own the DSR Platform Our current DSR process needs work. You will lead the roadmap to evolve this from a compliance checkbox into a scalable, automated system that handles access, deletion, and portability requests across all our data silos. 20% | Balance Privacy & Product You’ll define how we manage data and identity. The goal is to stay fully compliant (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) without sacrificing the user experience or our ability to deliver relevant content. 20% | Build the Foundation Partner with engineering to modernize our data architecture. You need to understand our data lineage, governance, and security well enough to guide architectural decisions across different business units. 20% | Make Privacy User-Friendly Stop treating privacy as a legal chore. You will design transparent, user-centric flows that actually help our readers understand their data, which in turn builds long-term brand trust. 20% | Cross-Functional Strategy You’ll be the bridge between Legal, AdTech, and Engineering. You need to be able to explain the technical risk to legal, and the regulatory requirements to our engineering leads. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree is preferred and/or equivalent experience. Experience: 5+ years in product management owning backend platforms. A candidate who has worked in data-heavy environments or managed compliance-related products or identity systems is required. Specific Knowledge, Skills, Certifications and Abilities: DSR Platform Expertise: Experience developing or expanding DSR systems. You understand the friction involved in verifying identities and synchronizing data across disconnected stacks and have a vision for automation. Technical Authority: Ability to lead technical discussions with engineers. You possess a strong grasp of APIs, data flow, and warehouse environments like BigQuery or Snowflake to guide fundamental architectural choices. Articulate Communication: Skill in distilling complex legal mandates or technical constraints into clear, actionable insights for leadership across Legal, Editorial, and Revenue teams. job.description: Job Title Senior Software Engineer 1, Picksy Services Job Description Picksy is our next-generation product discovery platform connecting shoppers with the things they love across thousands of retail partners. Users save, organize, and share products they're excited about — and our platform turns those signals into a deeply personalized shopping experience. This team owns the foundational product data, services, applications, and integrations that power the Picksy experience. Hybrid 3x per week In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week. You'll work closely with product owners, designers, and fellow engineers to translate requirements into prototypes and world-class features, and you'll be a go-to voice on architecture decisions and best practices across the team. Design and implement new services, APIs, and operational monitoring functions. Own production services end-to-end — investigating issues, resolving bottlenecks, and proactively identifying opportunities to improve reliability and reduce cost. Provide thorough, readable documentation for the services you own. Partner with engineers across the org to establish and align on shared best practices. Bring strong technical judgment to ambiguous problems, and deliver high-quality, complex services under tight timelines. Experience: 6+ years of relevant professional technology experience. Experience developing complex and highly available services running in a production environment with SLAs. Extensive knowledge of object-oriented and functional software design patterns, including those commonly used within large web application platforms. job.title: Social Operations Manager
job.description: Job Title Social Operations Manager Job Description About The Position People Inc. is seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and service-minded Social Operations Manager to join the Social Strategy and Operations team. This role will own and improve the operational systems, workflows, tools, access processes, and cross-functional support that enable our social editors to work efficiently across a large portfolio of brands. Reporting to the Sr. Director of Social Strategy, the Social Operations Manager will serve as a central operational partner to brand social teams, Sales, Paid Social, Security, IT, platform partners, vendors, and internal stakeholders. This person will manage day-to-day social operations, troubleshoot platform and tooling issues, oversee account and permissions processes, support employee onboarding and offboarding, and help ensure teams have the systems, documentation, and support needed to execute effectively. This is an operations-focused role. It does not involve content creation, publishing social posts, setting social strategy, or running organic social campaigns. Hybrid 3x a w eek- (New York, NY) In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week About The Positions Contributions: Operational Support & Coordination: Serve as the primary operational liaison between internal stakeholders, social platforms, and vendors. Provide day-to-day technical and operational support across social platforms and tools, including troubleshooting access, reporting, distribution, and account issues. Ongoing monitoring of the team's Slack channel to quickly address and help solve any issues raised by stakeholders in real time. Create, manage, and track support tickets with social platforms and vendors, ensuring timely follow-through and clear stakeholder communication. Proactively communicate platform issues, updates, resolutions, and process changes clearly to impacted teams. Maintain strong working knowledge of social platform and social publishing tool capabilities, limitations, operational requirements, and account structures. Lead coordination of enterprise-wide social operational initiatives spanning multiple brands, social teams, platform partners, and third-party vendors, ensuring complex, cross-functional work is planned, executed, communicated, and completed consistently at scale. Account Management, Access, and Governance: Handle setup, transfer, shutdown, and access management for accounts organization-wide. This involves establishing processes and workflows for integrating social media handles with new platform features, merging social media pages, and fixing content distribution problems. Onboarding and offboarding of new and departing employees. Partner with Security, IT, Legal, and relevant stakeholders to support access governance, account integrity, risk mitigation, and platform compliance. Sales and Paid Social Operational Support Help troubleshoot sponsored campaign setup, access,, tagging, permissions, and platform execution issues. Document operational requirements, dependencies, and timelines for paid and sponsored social workstreams. Social Tool Contracts & Renewals: Spearhead social vendor tool evaluations and contract renewals. Collaborate and coordinate across strategic sourcing, brands, social leadership and finance. Evaluate social tools and vendors against business and editorial needs, and ensure People Inc. is aligned with the best suite of tools to meet our business needs. Manage vendor contracts, seats, and invoices. Social Resources & Documentation: Maintain the People Inc. Social Resource Repository and ensure documentation, process guides, training materials, and operational resources remain accurate and up-to-date. Proactively identify documentation gaps and coordinate with subject matter experts to refresh or create needed materials. Coordinate social platform and social publishing tool trainings, ensuring strong stakeholder participation and adoption. Assemble, present and distribute recurring social operations updates, including platform news, process changes, and relevant operational guidance. Data and Reporting: Work with Business Insights, Data Operations and Marketing teams on social analytics and reporting, including overseeing the build out of key reports in Looker, QA’ing, and communicating to stakeholders as new data and reporting becomes available.
