Intro to Position

NPR is seeking a strategic and collaborative Salesforce Business Analyst to join a dedicated team focused on innovating and maintaining our enterprise Salesforce CRM. NPR’s Salesforce ecosystem is a critical driver of our organizational mission, powering operations that range from newsletter subscriptions and donor management to supporting our nationwide network of Member organizations and digital experiences for millions of public media listeners.

In this role, you will bridge the gap between business objectives and technical implementation. Working closely with diverse stakeholders, product managers, and development teams, you will strategically design, document, and refine our Salesforce data model and platform architecture. The ideal candidate is a natural problem-solver who can translate complex requirements into elegant, scalable Salesforce solutions, communicating seamlessly across varying levels of technical expertise.

  • Requirements Elicitation & Scoping: Facilitate collaborative workshops with stakeholders across NPR to elicit, analyze, and document business processes and functional requirements.
  • User Story Creation: Author clear, actionable user stories, acceptance criteria, and comprehensive process maps to guide development efforts.
  • Roadmap Alignment: Partner closely with Product Managers to evaluate incoming business requests, assess strategic value, and prioritize the Salesforce backlog.
  • Solution Design Collaboration: Collaborate with Senior Salesforce Administrators and Developers to design scalable solutions that optimize platform capabilities while safeguarding data model integrity.
  • Impact & Dependency Analysis: Partner with technical teams to assess how new requirements affect existing platform architectures, upstream/downstream integrations, and dependent business systems.
  • UAT & Enablement Leadership: Design user acceptance testing (UAT) scripts, coordinate testing cycles, and author end-user training materials to ensure seamless feature adoption.
  • Project Delivery Coordination: Serve as a functional lead on project teams, tracking project health, proactively managing delivery timelines, and keeping key stakeholders aligned.
  • Governance & Best Practices: Promote platform standards and Salesforce-native best practices across cross-divisional teams to minimize technical debt.
  • Relationship Management: Cultivate trusted partnerships with internal departments and cross-functional technology peers, fostering an environment of collaboration and mutual support.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

  • Experience: Minimum of four (4) years of dedicated experience in business analysis, requirements translation, and functional design within the Salesforce ecosystem.
  • Platform Knowledge: Solid working knowledge of core Salesforce capabilities, configuration options, security models, and declarative automation tools.
  • Project Delivery: Demonstrated success leading or driving functional phases of cross-functional Salesforce projects from discovery through to deployment.
  • Stakeholder Facilitation: Proven ability to facilitate requirements-gathering sessions with non-technical business partners and translate operational needs into technical specifications.
  • Platform Certification: Salesforce Certified Business Analyst certification

Preferred Qualifications

  • Ecosystem Tools: Familiarity with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, integrations, or related digital communication components

  • Communicative Clarity: Exceptional written and oral communication skills, with a proven ability to distill technical architectural concepts into plain-language value propositions for business leads.
  • Prioritization & Adaptability: Proven ability to manage multiple complex initiatives simultaneously, maintaining high-quality delivery amidst shifting timelines.
  • Analytical Problem Solving: Strong critical thinking skills, with an aptitude for identifying process bottlenecks and designing proactive, platform-native solutions.
  • Inclusive Collaboration: Strong interpersonal skills with a commitment to building collaborative, inclusive relationships across technical and non-technical teams.

job.title: Senior Director, Total Rewards
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

The Senior Director, Total Rewards leads, modernizes and directs the operational foundations of benefits and compensation programs at NPR, responsible for developing and driving a total rewards strategy that supports a culture of high performance to attract, reward, and retain top talent. Reporting to the SVP People and serving as a critical strategic partner to Finance, Legal, and broader NPR leadership, this position establishes total rewards as a pillar of NPR’s employer brand –redefining benefits, compensation, and systems to position NPR as an employer of choice. This role requires a unique balance of high-level strategic design, high-touch operational execution, and understanding.

The Senior Director of Total Rewards will bring deep expertise in compensation and benefits administration, strong knowledge of retirement plans, and will serve as a key partner to the HRIS/People Systems team to ensure that systems, data, eligibility rules, benefits deductions, reporting, and related processes accurately support total rewards programs. This role requires strong technical knowledge, keen attention to detail, and the ability to identify, audit, and help improve legacy processes and systems issues.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong understanding of benefits, operations, retirement plan administration, compensation and HR systems. They must be comfortable driving change, strengthening controls, improving processes and working cross-functionally with HRIS, Payroll, Finance, Legal, external vendors, auditors and senior organizational leadership.

Responsibilities

Transformation Leadership & Strategic HR Alignment

  • Functional Modernization: Drive the strategic transformation of Total Rewards and HRIS functions to align with NPR’s enterprise-wide organizational evolution, establishing scalable operating models, modern digital workflows, and progressive employee programs.
  • Leadership Partnership & Change Leadership: Partner closely with the SVP, People, HR People Partners, Finance, and leadership to align total rewards and systems strategy with overarching business goals and facilitate seamless organizational change.

Benefits

  • Benefits Strategy & Innovation: Lead the overall benefits strategy, incorporating a data-driven approach to recommendations and implementation of changes and improvements to our programs to maintain competitive advantage and meet the needs of the organization
  • Benefits & Retirement Program Administration: Provide strategic direction and oversight for all of the organization’s comprehensive benefits offerings, leave programs, and retirement plans, ensuring compliance testing, plan document accuracy, and successful audits.
  • Vendor & Broker Management: Oversee relationship management with health and benefit providers, third-party benefits advisors, and brokers. Direct the administration of benefit enrollment processes and leave programs.
  • Administration Issue Resolution: Proactively identify, troubleshoot, and resolve complex benefits and retirement plan administration issues, successfully correcting legacy errors, resolving vendor data discrepancies, closing process controls gaps, and resolving systems configuration concerns.

Compensation

  • Compensation Framework & Analytics: Develop and drive a unified compensation strategy aligned with broader HR objectives, utilizing robust data-driven analytics and modeling to evaluate market conditions, manage pay equity frameworks, and guide evidence-based salary decisions.
  • Annual Cycles & Budget Ownership: Direct the annual compensation planning process and own overall fiscal responsibilities for total rewards and systems budgets, partnering closely with Finance to manage resources cost-effectively.
  • Project Execution & Communications: Lead complex compensation and benefits projects from initial concept through design, modeling, and successful organization-wide implementation. Partner closely with the SVP of People, HR Business Partners, and additional stakeholders to ensure that total rewards programs are seamlessly integrated into broader HR and organizational strategies; author transparent communication materials and deliver structured training for leadership and staff on NPR's total rewards philosophy.
  • Ensure compliance with legal requirements and governance related to compensation and benefits programs.

Systems, Audits, & Data Compliance

  • People Systems Leadership: Direct the HRIS/People Systems team and establish the enterprise roadmap for UKG and integrated HR tools; ensure total rewards programs are accurately configured, administered, reported, and maintained within UKG; collaborate directly on system configuration, eligibility rules, and code setup to identify inaccuracies and improve data controls.
  • Data Auditing & Internal Controls: Develop standard operating procedures (SOPs), data validation routines, and process audit trails to proactively identify and resolve issues in legacy total rewards processes.
  • Total Rewards Compliance Leadership: Lead benefits, compensation, and systems compliance activities across the organization, ensuring compliance with any relevant federal, state, and local laws, including total reward regulations (e.g., ACA, Form 5500, and ERISA reporting).
  • Data Integrity & Reporting: Ensure total rewards data and reporting are accurate, timely, and useful for leadership decision-making, employee communications, and audit inquiries.

Team Leadership & Development

People Management: Direct, mentor, and coach the internal Total Rewards teams, establishing a culture of accountability, high accuracy, professional growth, and proactive customer service.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Professional Leadership & Strategy: 12 + years of progressive leadership experience across Total Rewards and HR Technology, with at least 6 years directly managing multidisciplinary HR teams.
  • Strategic Benefits Ownership: Proven track record designing and executing holistic benefit, retirement, and wellness strategies that enhance the employee value proposition in complex organizations.
  • Advanced HRIS Expertise: Proven experience managing, configuring, or optimizing enterprise-grade HRIS platforms, with specific, advanced expertise utilizing UKG (Ultimate Kronos Group) modules.
  • Team Leadership & Development: Demonstrated ability to lead and develop a high-performing team in a complex, collaborative organization
  • Benefits & Retirement Plan Administration: Comprehensive understanding of ERISA fiduciary duties, nondiscrimination testing, retirement plan audits, Form 5500 reporting, and working directly with plan recordkeepers and trustees across 401 (k) and 403b plans.
  • ERISA Fiduciary & Compliance Fluency: Robust knowledge of ERISA fiduciary responsibilities, nondiscrimination testing, plan audits, Form 5500 reporting, and retirement plan compliance; proven experience working directly with retirement plan recordkeepers, trustees, and investment advisors.
  • Analytical Auditing & Issue Resolution: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a proven ability to use data to drive decisions, audit complex datasets, and resolve data discrepancies, process and control gaps, and legacy system issues.
  • Compensation Practice Mastery: Strong understanding of compensation practices, including salary bands, market pricing, pay equity, incentive programs, and compensation governance.
  • Advisory Communication & Vendor Negotiation: Excellent interpersonal, oral and written communication skills, with the ability to provide strategic advice and counsel to senior leadership and negotiate effectively with insurance and benefit vendors.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Industry Certifications: Active professional designations such as CCP or CMS, SPHR or SHRM-CP or CEBS preferred
  • Collective Bargaining Experience: Experience developing and administering benefits and compensation programs in a unionized environment
  • Retirement Plan Compliance Testing: Experience supporting retirement plan audits, plan corrections, compliance testing, and plan governance

Key Competencies

  • Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy
  • Ability to understand how total rewards programs are operationalized through People Systems, Payroll, and vendor systems.
  • High degree of accountability, ownership, and follow-through
  • Ability to build credibility with the People Team, Finance, Legal, external vendors and senior leadership

Education Requirements

Bachelor's degree or equivalent in work experience.

Work Location & Requirements

Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. The employee will be required to be in the Washington, D.C. office at least 2 days a week. The employee must also reside in the D.C. Metropolitan Area.

Job Type
This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $192,000 - $230,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

job.title: Vice President, Individual and Institutional Giving
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

NPR is entering a period that requires sustained growth in philanthropic revenue and a fundraising organization built to deliver it consistently. The Vice President, Individual & Institutional Giving leads that organization: a team of approximately 20 across institutional giving, planned giving, individual giving, and donor recognition, accountable for ~$75M+ in annual revenue.

This is a systems leadership role. The VP does not carry a personal donor portfolio. Their leverage comes from the performance of five direct reports and the fundraisers beneath them — from pipeline discipline, coaching, and the standards they set for how NPR shows up with its donors. Reporting to the Chief Development Officer and partnering closely with the VP, Digital Revenue & Operations, the VP builds the infrastructure and the talent that make growth repeatable rather than episodic.

Responsibilities

Revenue Leadership

  • Own delivery of ~$75M+ in annual revenue across institutional, planned, and individual giving, with accountability for accurate forecasting and early warning when performance diverges from plan.
  • Set portfolio strategy and capacity targets across the team, allocating fundraiser time toward the relationships with the highest potential rather than the highest familiarity.
  • Partner with the CDO and Finance to build multi-year revenue projections grounded in pipeline evidence.

Pipeline & Moves Management

  • Own the moves management discipline across all frontline teams: stage definitions, advancement criteria, portfolio review cadence, and the accountability that makes them real.
  • Work with the Executive Director of Development Operations to build the reporting that gives every fundraiser and manager a clear view of their pipeline, and use it to drive weekly and monthly decisions rather than quarterly retrospectives.
  • Set the quality standard for the briefing materials, proposals, reports, and engagement strategies the team produces, so that every executive donor meeting has a defined purpose and a defined next step.
  • Diagnose where relationships stall and address the cause — whether that is skill, capacity, strategy, or a gap in what NPR can offer.

Team Leadership & Fundraiser Development

  • Lead and develop five direct reports across institutional giving, planned giving, individual giving, and recognition, holding each accountable for team performance while building their capability as managers.
  • Define what excellent fundraising looks like at NPR and build the coaching, training, and evaluation practices that produce it, with clear expectations by level and visible paths for advancement.
  • Develop fundraisers into compelling representatives of NPR — people who understand journalism deeply, can articulate what it costs and why it matters, and can hold a substantive conversation with a sophisticated donor.
  • Attend donor meetings regularly as coach and observer, present to develop the fundraiser rather than to own the relationship.
  • Partner with the CDO and the People team on hiring, performance management, and org design as the team scales.

Stewardship & Donor Recognition

  • Oversee the design and rollout of a tiered donor recognition system that works across giving channels and can be adopted organization-wide.
  • Build stewardship practices that treat retention and upgrade as designed outcomes rather than byproducts of goodwill.

Capacity & Efficiency

  • Identify where AI and automation can absorb the research, preparation, drafting, and analysis that consume frontline time, and redirect the capacity created toward the work that requires a human being: relationship depth, judgment in the room, and the ability to make NPR’s mission land.
  • Bring fluency with current AI tools and the judgment to distinguish genuine leverage from novelty, and build a team culture where adoption is expected and evaluated.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with the VP, Digital Revenue & Operations to create a coherent donor experience across digital and frontline giving, with clear handoffs as donors move between channels.
  • Work with Member Station colleagues and the Network Growth team to coordinate donor engagement across the public media system.
  • Align fundraising priorities with editorial and executive leadership so that what the team is selling reflects where NPR is going.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

In the first year, you will:

  • Install pipeline standards. Define stages, advancement criteria, and conversion benchmarks across institutional, planned, and individual giving, and establish the review cadence that holds the team to them.
  • Define fundraising excellence. Publish skill expectations by level across all frontline roles, with an assessment approach and a development plan for every fundraiser on the team.
  • Launch tiered recognition. Design and implement a donor recognition structure built for adoption across NPR.
  • Free up frontline capacity. Identify the highest-cost manual work across the team, deploy AI and automation against it, and demonstrate the hours returned to donor-facing activity.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 15+ years of professional experience, including 7+ years leading multi-team organizations and managing through managers.
  • 5+ years in development. Experience in enterprise sales, executive search, or another discipline built on long-cycle, trust-dependent relationships is a strong substitute for a longer fundraising tenure, and we encourage those candidates to apply.
  • Demonstrated accountability for a revenue program of comparable scale, with evidence of sustained year-over-year growth.
  • Proven track record of building pipeline systems and coaching practices that improved team performance, distinct from personal production.
  • Fluency with pipeline data and CRM reporting, and a habit of using it to make decisions about where people spend their time.
  • Working fluency with AI tools and a track record of finding practical efficiency gains with them.
  • Strong listening, writing, and speaking skills, with the ability to represent a complex organization to sophisticated audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • An understanding of complex fundraising organizations or federated nonprofit models.
  • An understanding of media/public broadcasting organizations and the relationship between NPR and its Member Stations.
  • Experience leading teams through a period of rapid growth or structural change.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in work experience required.

Work Location & Requirements

  • NPR Remote-Permitted: This is a remote-permitted role. This role is based out of our Washington, D.C. office, but the employee may choose to work on a remote basis from a location that NPR approves. You will have the option of working (a) remotely from a location of your choosing within the United States that is supported by NPR; (b) on-site at an NPR facility, based on the availability of desks and approval from NPR; or (c) a combination of both. Regardless of where you choose to work from, you may be expected to travel to other locations from time to time to perform the duties of your position.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $216,000-$240,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

Does this sound like you? If so, we want to hear from you.

job.title: Artist Marketing Director, Southeast Asia
job.description: About ONErpm Founded in 2010, ONErpm is a global music solutions company with 43 offices and studios in 35+ countries with over 530 staff members across the world, with significant presence in Brazil, the U.S., Europe, and other markets. ONErpm encompasses distribution, label solutions, content production, publishing, and an innovative marketing group that includes in-house advertising and influencer agencies, ONErpm has a proven track record of providing local and global support to artists and creators at any stage of their careers. About The Role The Artist Marketing Director, Southeast Asia (Global Level 4) is responsible for leading and managing the Regional Marketing Project Management team. This role defines and executes the country-specific artistic marketing strategy in close collaboration with the head of Asia and the Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), ensuring alignment with global business objectives while addressing local market opportunities. The Artist Marketing Director develops, oversees, and evaluates integrated marketing and communication strategies, including campaign planning and execution, sales promotion initiatives, advertising agency management, promotional activities, and market research. The role is accountable for driving market share growth, maximizing artist visibility and audience engagement, and enhancing the effectiveness of artist marketing initiatives across digital and social media platforms. This position also provides strategic leadership on local market trends, consumer behavior, and competitive dynamics, translating insights into impactful marketing programs that support client and artist success. This role reports directly to the Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) of ONErpm and the head of Asia. Responsibilities: Direct the evolution and implementation of artist and release marketing frameworks, spearheading high-impact album and single launches and consumer-centric digital campaigns designed to accelerate audience expansion and fan engagement. Act as the primary strategic conduit between artists, management, and ONErpm, cultivating robust professional relationships to ensure cohesive alignment on marketing targets and project execution. Collaborate cross-functionally with label services and internal business units to engineer and deploy innovative marketing programs that bolster artist releases, catalog optimization, and specialized initiatives. Lead the conceptualization, planning, and management of creative marketing strategies, ensuring all campaigns are synchronized with artist vision, market trends, and organizational priorities. Govern the development of project roadmaps, financial budgets, and critical deliverables, orchestrating departmental efforts to guarantee the seamless and timely delivery of marketing milestones. Assess campaign efficacy, market shifts, consumer behavior, and competitive intelligence to uncover growth opportunities, refine strategy, and deliver actionable data-driven insights to leadership. Coordinate and manage alliances with external stakeholders, including PR firms, radio promotion specialists, booking agents, and industry partners, to optimize campaign reach and artist visibility. Provide mentorship and strategic direction to Marketing Project Managers and Coordinators, driving team productivity, career growth, and operational high performance. Manage the talent lifecycle—including recruitment, onboarding, and continuous training—to cultivate a sophisticated, high-performing, and collaborative marketing culture. Partner with senior executives to assess and authorize resource allocation for project management, supporting international marketing objectives and global expansion. Co-manage strategic digital alliances with top-tier platforms like Meta and TikTok, alongside emerging digital entities, in coordination with the Digital leadership team. Proactively identify, pitch, and secure premium digital marketing placements, original content opportunities, and promotional visibility for the ONErpm roster through key platform integrations. Establish and fortify strategic relationships with external industry bodies, including PROs, media organizations, and relevant music industry stakeholders. Ensure all marketing frameworks, partnerships, and tactical initiatives contribute meaningfully to artist development, fan acquisition, revenue streams, and market share growth. Qualifications Minimum 7 years of experience in artistic marketing or related roles within the music, entertainment, or media industry. Proven experience leading local marketing teams. Demonstrated success developing and executing large-scale marketing campaigns with measurable results. Deep understanding of music marketing, streaming ecosystems, audience growth strategies, and fan engagement. Experience managing cross-functional projects and collaborating with artists, managers, labels, agencies, and platform partners. Strong analytical skills with experience interpreting campaign performance data, KPIs, and ROI metrics. Experience overseeing media budgets, forecasting, and campaign optimization across multiple markets. Knowledge of influencer marketing, social media trends, and emerging digital platforms. Excellent communication, leadership, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Experience with CRM, audience data collection, and fan acquisition strategies including email, SMS, and retargeting. Ability to work effectively across diverse cultures, teams, and international markets. Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities with a results-driven mindset. Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, Music Business, or a related field preferred. Ability to communicate fluently and effectively in English and one or more Southeast Asian languages (Mandarin, Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Malaysia, Tagalog, Thai, Vietnamese)

job.title: Championship Department Intern
job.description: Join a team of proud, passionate, and caring people that together share their diverse talents and backgrounds to serve our members and grow the game of golf. Being at the PGA of America means you are supported, respected, and appreciated for your contributions. This position will offer exposure to the competition, operations, administration, and volunteer program at our various Championships. RESPONSIBILITIES (Specific areas of responsibility include but are not limited to): Provide operational function/support in course preparations, which may include but not limited to course marking, rope and stake installation, course signage, and on-course leader boards. Provide administrative function/support, computer scoring operations (Golf Genius), and communication support for PGA Member, Spectator, and Amateur Championships as assigned. Assist with all Championship event shipping and receiving. Assist with organizing set-ups of temporary on-site Championship Offices. Assist with Championship volunteer operations. When the event is completed, assist the Championship Department Staff with the breakdown of the course, offices, volunteer headquarters, and other areas to be determined at site. Assist with unpacking and packing the semi-trailers for events the intern is working on. Assist Championship Department Staff elsewhere when needed. INCLUSION: Employees are expected to contribute to a respectful and inclusive team environment by welcoming and respecting others’ beliefs, backgrounds, identities, abilities, and individuality to help ensure a supportive and engaging experience for Association Members, partners, customers, and guests. PGA of America respects the uniqueness of each employee and offers everyone the means to find their place and thrive. SHARED VALUES: Embody the organization's shared values and help ensure the organization's values-based culture thrives by proactively identifying and addressing any shared values, challenges, and opportunities you are experiencing. Supervision: No supervisory responsibilities. Financial Responsibilities: No financial responsibilities. Education and Experience: High School Diploma, or equivalent. Must be a rising Junior or above enrolled in a degree program or a recent college graduate. Golf background or strong interest in golf required Skills, Knowledge and Abilities: Must have knowledge of business operations with an emphasis in administrative support, finance and/or operations. Working knowledge of computer design software such as Adobe Creative Suite. Working knowledge of Gmail, Google Drive, Google Sheets, and Google Docs. Basic fluency in artificial intelligence (AI) tools and concepts. This includes using AI to enhance business operations and drive innovation, enabling us to better serve our Members and stakeholders. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position. job.title: Sr Mgr, Talent Acquisition - US Corporate & Commercial
job.description: Working at QVC Group means joining a live social shopping company with incredible teams, ambitious projects and amazing careers. QVC Group, Inc. is a Fortune 500 company with six leading retail brands - QVC®, HSN®, Ballard Designs®, Frontgate®, Garnet Hill® and Grandin Road. Your Opportunity, Your Team As Senior Manager, Talent Acquisition, you'll lead a significant portion of our TA function, guiding Managers and senior recruiting professionals as they deliver talent for the business. This isn't a role where you'll spend your days working a req list. You'll own the talent acquisition strategy for your area, from sourcing channel mix and pipeline development to employer brand activation and the operating model that ties it all together, and you'll build the systems and team capability that make great recruiting repeatable at scale. You'll report to the Senior Director, US Talent Acquisition, and you'll operate as a true business partner to functional leaders and HR leadership, advising on talent strategy, market dynamics, and hiring decisions at a level that shapes how the organization designs itself. You'll also drive our shift toward proactive talent acquisition, embedding a talent advisor mindset across your team so that recruiters show up as labor market analysts, career coaches, hiring strategists, and process change agents. If you're energized by building teams, frameworks, and capability rather than simply filling roles, and you want to help transform how a Fortune 500 company finds and hires talent, keep reading. Where You'll Work This role is hybrid and will require you to be onsite at our West Chester, PA headquarters (Studio Park) several days per month (onsite days are predetermined and standard across the company). Job seekers must reside in one of the following states to be considered: Pennsylvania, New Jersey, or Delaware. Relocation assistance is not available for this role. What You'll Do Lead and develop a team of TA professionals, setting the standards, coaching performance, and building the bench of future recruiting leaders. Own the proactive talent acquisition strategy for your area, including sourcing channels, pipeline development, talent community building, and employer brand activation. Advise senior business and HR leaders on talent strategy, labor market dynamics, and hiring decisions, earning a seat at the table on workforce planning and organizational design. Lead TA business planning for your area, including headcount demand forecasting, recruiter capacity modeling, and alignment to workforce plans. Build the KPI frameworks, capability programs, and accountability structures that make consultative, data-driven recruiting the norm across your team. Identify systemic gaps in how the function operates, design solutions, and drive implementation through your leadership team. Develop team capability in advanced sourcing, business partnering, data literacy, inclusive hiring practices, and candidate experience design. Partner with Total Rewards on compensation strategy and offer competitiveness, bringing forward hiring market patterns that should inform comp decisions. Set standards for full utilization of TA technology and data-driven recruiting practices, and hold leaders accountable for translating tools into measurable outcomes. Establish vendor governance for your area, holding search firms and platform vendors accountable to defined performance standards and ROI. Lead or co-lead cross-functional projects spanning process re-engineering, technology implementation, and organizational capability. Represent QVC Group externally in industry forums, employer brand events, and senior recruiting networks, strengthening our market presence and talent pipelines. Step into a small number of high-priority or sensitive searches when your direct involvement adds real value. What You'll Bring 10+ years of recruiting experience, including at least 5 years in progressively senior TA management roles. Experience managing managers and leading recruiting teams through other leaders, including coaching, performance management, and succession planning. A track record of driving TA transformation, whether shifting a team toward proactive sourcing, redesigning operating models, or building new capability at scale. Strong business partnering skills, with demonstrated credibility advising HR and senior business leaders on talent strategy. Fluency with recruiting data and analytics, and comfort using both to coach performance and influence decisions. Experience with TA technology, workforce planning, and organizational change. Commitment to inclusive sourcing and hiring practices. #LI-AI1 Our Total Rewards package includes benefits you’ll love such as competitive compensation, paid time off, an employee assistance program, parental leave, paid volunteer hours, and amazing company discounts! In our US market, you can also expect health care benefits starting on day 1, 401(k), and tuition reimbursement benefits. Scripps is seeking an experienced Director, Engineering - Networks to oversee our cutting-edge broadcast infrastructure in Atlanta. This is your opportunity to lead a talented team of engineering specialists while shaping the future of our technical operations across studio equipment, post-production facilities, video file storage, satellite earth stations, and critical power protection systems. In this role, you'll combine deep technical expertise in IP networks and television operations with strategic leadership to drive innovation and excellence. If you're passionate about broadcast technology and thrive in a fast-paced environment where your decisions directly impact our ability to deliver world-class content, we want to hear from you. job.title: Executive Reporter, KGUN
job.description: At KGUN 9, we're looking for a storyteller's storyteller. This is a unique opportunity for an accomplished journalist who is ready to take the next step from creating great stories to shaping the people who tell them. Part coach, part manager, part mentor, part researcher, and sometimes even photographer or videographer, you'll be the driving force behind elevating storytelling across our newsroom. You'll work alongside talented reporters and MMJs, helping them uncover deeper angles, strengthen their craft, and find new ways to connect with our community. If you're passionate about journalism, energized by developing others, and excited to lead through a transformational time in local news, this role offers the chance to leave a lasting impact on both our audience and the next generation of storytellers. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Lead and elevate the storytelling skills and capabilities of reporters and MMJs across the newsroom. Mentor, coach, and develop journalists at all experience levels through regular feedback and guidance. Collaborate with newsroom leadership to execute a cohesive content strategy centered on authentic, impactful storytelling. Oversee story writing and content development across broadcast, digital, and social platforms. Review content and provide timely, constructive feedback that drives continuous improvement. Develop and implement efficient workflows and editorial processes that support multiple news programs and platforms. Ensure all reporting and content meet high journalistic standards, ethical guidelines, and legal requirements. Foster a culture of trust, accountability, and collaboration among reporters, photographers, and newsroom staff. Identify innovative approaches to storytelling that deepen audience engagement and community connection. Provide on-air and multi-platform coverage of breaking news and major events as needed. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Bachelor's degree in journalism, communications, or a related field preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Generally 7+ years of professional experience in journalism, reporting, content leadership, or a related field preferred. Demonstrated experience leading projects, mentoring talent, or driving editorial excellence in a newsroom environment. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Proven expertise in compelling, impactful storytelling across multiple platforms. Strong editorial judgment and a thorough understanding of journalistic ethics, standards, and libel laws. Deep curiosity about the communities, issues, and events that shape local, national, and global conversations. A strong understanding of content strategy and audience engagement best practices. Excellent communication, coaching, and relationship-building skills. The ability to thrive in a fast-paced newsroom and make sound decisions under deadline pressure. Adaptability, initiative, and a collaborative approach to problem-solving. Flexibility to work a variety of shifts, including nights, weekends, early mornings, and holidays. OUR TEAM: At KGUN 9, you'll join a passionate team of journalists dedicated to serving Southern Arizona through trusted, community-focused reporting. We value collaboration, innovation, and continuous learning, and we believe our best work happens when diverse perspectives come together. Our newsroom is filled with talented storytellers who support one another, embrace creativity, and share a commitment to journalistic excellence. WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Tucson offers an exceptional blend of natural beauty, vibrant culture, and outdoor adventure. Nestled among stunning mountain ranges and surrounded by breathtaking desert landscapes, the city boasts more than 300 days of sunshine each year. Whether you're hiking scenic trails, exploring world-renowned national parks, enjoying local festivals, or dining at Tucson's celebrated restaurants, there's always something to discover. As a UNESCO City of Gastronomy, Tucson is known for its rich culinary heritage, thriving arts scene, and welcoming community spirit. job.title: Executive Reporter, WKBW
job.description: Executive Reporter, WKBW WKBW, the ABC affiliate in Buffalo, New York, owned by The E.W. Scripps Company, is searching for an Executive Reporter to help lead our newsroom into the future. This is a unique opportunity for an accomplished journalist who excels at both storytelling and leadership. As Executive Reporter, you'll be a newsroom coach, content strategist, and trusted editorial voice, helping reporters and multimedia journalists elevate their work while contributing your own impactful journalism across platforms. You'll collaborate with newsroom leaders to shape content that matters to Western New York, develop journalists at every stage of their careers, and champion innovative storytelling that strengthens our connection with audiences. The ideal candidate is passionate about local journalism, believes in the power of enterprise reporting, and is energized by helping others do their best work. You'll play a critical role in advancing WKBW's mission of serving our community with authentic, meaningful, and impactful storytelling. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Lead, mentor, and develop reporters and multimedia journalists, helping them grow as storytellers across broadcast, digital, streaming, and social platforms. Partner with newsroom leadership to execute a content strategy focused on audience needs, community impact, and meaningful journalism. Coach reporters on story development, enterprise reporting, writing, presentation, and newsroom best practices. Review stories and provide actionable feedback to improve content quality, storytelling, and audience engagement. Help identify and develop high-impact enterprise, investigative, and community-focused stories. Foster a culture of collaboration, innovation, accountability, and continuous learning. Serve as a trusted editorial leader, ensuring content meets the highest standards of journalistic ethics, accuracy, and fairness. Work closely with producers, assignment editors, digital teams, and newsroom leaders to maximize the reach and impact of content. Build confidence and trust among reporters, photographers, producers, and other newsroom staff. Provide on-air and multi-platform coverage of significant stories, breaking news, and special projects as needed. May pitch, shoot, write, edit, and produce content across platforms. Perform other duties as assigned. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: BS/BA in Journalism, Communications, or a related discipline preferred, or equivalent years of experience. Generally, 7+ years of experience in journalism, reporting, or newsroom leadership preferred. Experience coaching, mentoring, or leading journalists in a fast-paced newsroom environment preferred. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: A proven track record of impactful storytelling and enterprise reporting. Strong news judgment and a deep understanding of journalistic ethics, media law, and newsroom standards. Passion for coaching and developing journalists. A commitment to audience-first journalism and serving the needs of the Buffalo and Western New York community. Demonstrated ability to collaborate across teams and influence without direct authority. Experience creating content for multiple platforms, including broadcast, digital, social, and streaming. Strong communication, leadership, and relationship-building skills. Curiosity, creativity, and a drive to continuously improve storytelling and newsroom performance. Ability to work a variety of shifts, including nights, weekends, early mornings, and holidays. WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY: Buffalo is a city on the rise, combining big-city amenities with a strong sense of community and affordability that's hard to find elsewhere. Nestled along the shores of Lake Erie and just minutes from Niagara Falls, Western New York offers stunning outdoor recreation, vibrant neighborhoods, passionate sports fans, and a growing food and arts scene. Whether you're exploring the city's waterfront, enjoying world-class architecture, catching a Bills or Sabres game, or spending a weekend in the Finger Lakes, Buffalo offers an exceptional quality of life. At WKBW, you'll join a newsroom with a long tradition of impactful journalism and community service. We are committed to producing meaningful stories that matter to the people of Western New York while embracing innovation across broadcast, digital, streaming, and social platforms. If you're passionate about local journalism and helping shape the future of storytelling, Buffalo is a great place to build your career and make a difference. #LI-SM2 #LI-ONSITE COMPENSATION RANGE: Annual Salary: $85,000.00 - $120,000 Pursuant to state and local salary transparency laws, the salary range posted is specific to candidates who will perform this work in New York. job.title: Lead AI Architect (Onsite - Hybrid)
job.description: The E.W. Scripps Company is seeking a Lead AI Architect to d esign and implement enterprise-scale AI solutions with a strong engineering foundation, bringing deep technical expertise in agentic systems, developer tooling, and AI platform integration. Contribute to the architectural strategy for AI-powered applications — including agent frameworks, tool ecosystems, and model provider integrations — and translate business requirements into production-grade systems built to last. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Define and own AI solution architectures spanning agentic workflows, MCP server infrastructure, and multi-model orchestration. Lead the design and deployment of complex RAG architectures and vector database strategies to support enterprise data retrieval. Architect and implement MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and tool integrations, emphasizing advanced function calling and structured output schemas. Drive integration with major model providers (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) and define standards for model selection, routing, and fallback. Establish engineering patterns for AI observability, prompt engineering, and rigorous AI evaluation frameworks to ensure reliability. Collaborate with engineering, product, and platform teams to deliver integrated AI solutions within existing software ecosystems. Ensure scalability, security, and maintainability through sound software architecture principles. Guide prototyping and proof-of-concept efforts; define technical evaluation criteria for emerging AI tools and frameworks. Present technical solutions and recommendations to senior stakeholders in a clear and compelling way. Mentor peers and establish best practices in AI engineering, agent design, and tooling. Uphold and define security, compliance, and responsible AI standards, specifically addressing OWASP LLM Top 10 risks, prompt injection, and PII leakage. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: BS/BA in Computer in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred Generally, 8+ years of experience in related field preferred Experience in AI/agent development strongly preferred Relevant certifications (AWS, Azure, cloud AI services) a plus Experience in the Media and Broadcast domain is a plus WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Advanced experience building and deploying production AI applications with a software engineering mindset. Hands-on expertise designing and deploying AI agents using frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or similar. Deep understanding of RAG implementation patterns and vector database optimization. Proficiency setting up and managing MCP servers and defining tool schemas for LLM tool-use integrations. Strong experience integrating with cloud-hosted model providers — particularly AWS Bedrock and Azure AI Service. Proficiency in at least one backend programming language (Python, TypeScript/Node.js, Java, etc.) for building production AI systems. Familiarity with REST/GraphQL APIs, event-driven architectures, and containerized deployments (Docker, Kubernetes). Experience with CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, and developer tooling in cloud environments. Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences. Understanding of AI safety, prompt security, and responsible AI practices. Awareness or experience with LLM fine-tuning is a plus. #LI-SM 2 #LI-Onsite If you are a current Scripps employee, please do not apply on this site. job.description: Are you a technical leader ready to take the helm of broadcast operations? As Manager, Station Broadcasting, you'll be at the center of everything that keeps our station on-air and thriving. This role is critical to ensuring seamless daily operations, maintaining cutting-edge broadcast systems, and leading a team dedicated to technical excellence. job.title: Multi-Media Managing Editor, WKBW
job.description: Multi-Media Managing Editor, WKBW WKBW, the E.W. Scripps ABC Station in Buffalo, NY, is searching for a Multi-Media Managing Editor to help lead a new era of local news. We're looking for a newsroom leader who understands that today's audiences expect news wherever they are, whether that's on a streaming channel, a phone, social media, or television. You'll be at the center of our operation, helping drive a 24/7 news stream while ensuring the newsroom stays connected, informed, and focused on the stories that matter most. This role is part coach, part editor, and part conductor. You'll help reporters and MMJs tell stronger stories, make smart decisions in the moment, and find creative ways to connect our journalism with the communities we serve. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Lead the daily execution of WKBW's streaming and digital news coverage, ensuring audiences have access to timely, relevant content around the clock. Serve as the newsroom's central information hub, helping coordinate coverage plans, breaking news response, and content priorities. Coach and develop reporters and MMJs to elevate storytelling across digital, streaming, social, and broadcast platforms. Collaborate with newsroom leadership to execute audience-focused content strategies that drive engagement and community impact. Oversee the writing, editing, and publishing of stories across all platforms while maintaining quality and consistency. Provide timely and constructive feedback that helps journalists strengthen their reporting, writing, and presentation skills. Develop and refine workflows that support multiple news products, including streaming, digital, social, and broadcast content. Ensure all content meets the highest standards of journalistic ethics, accuracy, fairness, and legal compliance. Help identify opportunities for enterprise and accountability reporting that resonate with local audiences. Support breaking news coverage and provide multi-platform content leadership when news demands immediate action. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Seven or more years of experience in journalism, digital content, newsroom leadership, streaming, or a related field preferred. Proven experience managing content in a fast-paced newsroom environment and making sound editorial decisions under deadline pressure. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Deep roots in digital journalism, streaming content, and audience engagement strategies. Strong understanding of broadcast-style storytelling and how to adapt stories across platforms. Demonstrated expertise in coaching journalists and helping teams produce stronger, more impactful work. Exceptional editorial judgment and knowledge of journalistic ethics, media law, and libel standards. Curiosity about the communities, issues, and people that shape the stories we cover every day. Strong organizational and communication skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. A collaborative leadership style that builds trust and encourages innovation throughout the newsroom. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment where priorities can shift quickly. Flexibility to work a variety of shifts, including nights, weekends, early mornings, and holidays when news coverage requires it. OUR TEAM: WKBW is home to journalists who care deeply about serving Buffalo and Western New York. We're a collaborative team of reporters, photographers, producers, digital content creators, and newsroom leaders who believe local journalism should inform, connect, and strengthen the communities we serve. Our team is committed to impactful storytelling, breaking news excellence, accountability journalism, and meaningful community engagement. We embrace innovation, encourage new ideas, and support one another as we evolve for the future of local news. WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Buffalo offers a unique combination of affordability, opportunity, and quality of life. Located on the shores of Lake Erie and just minutes from Niagara Falls, Buffalo is a city experiencing continued growth and revitalization while maintaining its strong sense of community and hometown pride. Whether you're exploring the waterfront, cheering on the Bills, Sabres, or Bandits, enjoying the city's renowned food scene, hiking nearby parks, or taking weekend trips throughout Western New York and Southern Ontario, Buffalo offers something for everyone. It's a community that values local journalism and provides countless opportunities to tell stories that make a real impact. At WKBW, you'll have the opportunity to lead coverage in a market known for passionate audiences, strong community connections, and stories that matter. #LI-SM2 #LI-Onsite COMPENSATION RANGE: Annual Salary: $85,000.00 - $120,000 Pursuant to state and local salary transparency laws, the salary range posted is specific to candidates who will perform this work in New York. We're looking for a Multimedia Journalist who wants to immerse themselves in the community, chase meaningful stories, and bring them to life across multiple platforms. From breaking news and in-depth features to live reporting from the field, you'll be at the center of the stories that matter most to our viewers. If you're energized by journalism, inspired by mountain landscapes, and excited about making a real impact in a close-knit community, we'd love to meet you. Write compelling, accurate stories that meet broadcast and digital editorial standards. Shoot engaging video and capture still photography to support storytelling across platforms. Edit video content for on-air broadcasts, digital channels, and social media. Deliver live reports from the scene of breaking news, community events, and enterprise stories. Appear on-air for interviews, stand-ups, and story narration. Collaborate closely with photographers, producers, and digital teams to create impactful coverage. Assist in preparing daily newscasts and multimedia content plans. Consistently produce content that informs, connects, and serves the communities of western Montana. Experience with videography and non-linear editing systems. Working knowledge of broadcast-quality camera equipment. Experience editing on Final Cut Pro or similar editing platforms. Proficiency with newsroom computer systems and digital publishing tools. Ability to post and optimize content for websites and digital platforms. A self-starter mindset with excellent time management and organizational skills. Sound news judgment and the ability to work effectively under tight deadlines. A collaborative approach and passion for community-focused storytelling. Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds of equipment when needed. We are looking for someone who knows how to find stories you won’t find anywhere else. San Diego’s sunny, mild weather all year makes it perfect if you love being outdoors. You’ve got gorgeous beaches, fun parks, and tons of things to do—from great restaurants to festivals and live music. This is a strong newsroom with great, supportive leadership. Apply today! WHAT YOU'LL DO: Receive assignments or evaluate news leads and news tips to develop story ideas. Gather and verify factual information regarding stories through interview, observation, and research. Organize material, determine emphasis, and write story according to prescribed editorial style and format standards. Shoot video and still photos to illustrate stories. Edit, or assist in editing, videos for all multimedia platforms. Appear on television program when conducting taped interview or narration. Give live reports from site of event or mobile broadcast unit. Work cooperatively with photographer assigned to story, if one is assigned. Assist news producer in preparing newscast. Assist online staff in preparing for multimedia stories. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Bachelors degree in broadcast journalism or related degree or equivalent years of experience. Generally, 3+ years experience in related field preferred. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Computer literacy required, including newsroom computer systems. Videography and non-linear editing experience preferred. Knowledge of broadcast quality camera equipment. Edit video on Final Cut Pro editing systems, or similar equipment. Strong broadcast and AP style writing skills. Proficient at posting content to various websites. Self-motivated and able to work in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds. job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KPAX
job.description: At KPAX, we believe local journalism has the power to inform, connect, and strengthen communities. As a Multimedia Journalist, you'll play a key role in telling the stories that matter most to viewers across western Montana. From breaking news and community events to impactful enterprise reporting, you'll research, shoot, write, edit, and deliver compelling content across multiple platforms. You'll have the opportunity to build trusted relationships, uncover meaningful stories, and help audiences stay informed wherever they consume news. If you're a passionate storyteller who thrives in a fast-paced environment, we'd love to hear from you. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Develop story ideas by evaluating news leads, tips, community trends, and daily assignments. Research, gather, and verify information through interviews, observation, and independent reporting. Write clear, accurate, and engaging stories aligned with broadcast and digital editorial standards. Capture high-quality video and still photography to support news coverage. Edit video content for television broadcasts, digital platforms, and social media channels. Deliver live reports from the field and provide real-time coverage of breaking news and community events. Appear on-air for story narration, interviews, and newscast presentations. Collaborate with photographers, producers, and newsroom colleagues to create impactful content. Support newscast preparation by contributing story elements, updates, and editorial input. Work closely with digital and online teams to enhance multimedia storytelling across platforms. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience. Three or more years of relevant journalism, reporting, or multimedia storytelling experience preferred. Valid driver's license with a good driving record and the ability to provide proof of insurance meeting company requirements. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Strong broadcast and AP-style writing skills with a commitment to accuracy and storytelling excellence. Experience with videography and non-linear video editing platforms. Knowledge of professional broadcast camera equipment and field production techniques. Proficiency editing video using Final Cut Pro or comparable editing systems. Comfortable posting and managing content across websites and digital platforms. Strong computer skills, including experience with newsroom computer systems. Excellent news judgment, time management, and organizational abilities. A self-starter mentality with the ability to work independently and collaboratively. Confidence working under pressure in a fast-paced, deadline-driven newsroom environment. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds as needed in support of field reporting and production activities. OUR TEAM: At KPAX, you'll join a collaborative newsroom dedicated to delivering trusted local journalism. Our team brings together experienced journalists, creative storytellers, and passionate community advocates who support one another and share a commitment to serving viewers with integrity. We value diverse perspectives, innovative ideas, and a culture where curiosity, teamwork, and professional growth thrive. WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Nestled in the heart of western Montana, Missoula offers an unmatched combination of outdoor adventure, vibrant arts and culture, and a strong sense of community. Surrounded by mountains, rivers, and scenic trails, it's a destination for hiking, skiing, mountain biking, fishing, and year-round exploration. Beyond its natural beauty, Missoula is home to a thriving downtown, local breweries, live music, unique restaurants, and the University of Montana. Whether you're looking for outdoor recreation, cultural experiences, or a welcoming place to call home, Missoula provides an exceptional quality of life and endless opportunities to make an impact both personally and professionally. #LI-SM2 #LI-Onsite If you are a current Scripps employee, please do not apply on this site. job.title: Producer, KTVQ
job.description: At KTVQ, we believe local journalism has the power to inform, connect, and strengthen the communities we serve. As a Producer, you'll play a critical role in shaping the stories that matter most to viewers across Montana, creating compelling newscasts and digital content that keep audiences engaged and informed. You'll collaborate with talented journalists, anchors, editors, and newsroom leaders to deliver accurate, impactful coverage every day. This role is ideal for a passionate storyteller who thrives in a fast-paced environment, loves local news, and can confidently make decisions under deadline pressure. If you're ready to help lead a newsroom dedicated to serving its community, we'd love to hear from you. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Develop and organize daily newscasts and local programming. Write compelling stories, teases, and showcase content that engage viewers. Collaborate with reporters, anchors, assignment editors, and newsroom leadership to determine coverage priorities. Advance stories through research, planning, and creative storytelling approaches. Enhance content with graphics, video, data, and station branding elements. Make timely editorial decisions in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Oversee live broadcasts and adjust content as breaking news develops. Perform desktop editing to ensure polished and accurate presentations. Publish and manage content across station websites and digital platforms. Support newsroom operations and contribute to special projects as assigned. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience. Two or more years of experience in a newsroom, content production, or related field preferred. Understanding of journalistic standards, ethics, and applicable media laws preferred. Self-motivation, initiative, and a willingness to adapt to changing news conditions. Working knowledge of journalistic ethics, libel laws, and newsroom best practices. Experience using web analytics and digital audience insights to inform content decisions. Proficiency with newsroom computer systems; experience with Microsoft Office is a plus. Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, holidays, and other hours as news coverage demands. OUR TEAM: The KTVQ newsroom is made up of passionate journalists, storytellers, and content creators committed to serving viewers throughout the region. We value collaboration, creativity, curiosity, and accountability. Our team brings together diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, creating an environment where great ideas thrive and community-focused journalism makes a real impact. job.title: Regional Digital Sales Manager, Hybrid
job.description: Are you a dynamic sales leader ready to drive digital revenue growth and shape the future of local media advertising? We're seeking an experienced Digital Sales Manager who will lead our digital sales strategy, develop our sales team, and deliver innovative advertising solutions that help local businesses thrive. This is your opportunity to make a significant impact on our station's success while building a high-performing team. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Collaborate with DOS and other sales managers and departments to accomplish the objectives of each assigned station. Full responsibility for digital revenue, including establishing and achieving monthly, quarterly, and annual digital sales goals. Develop and execute local digital sales strategy and revenue plan. Make business decisions regarding the profitability of the sales organization as well as specific sales proposals and offerings. Serve as the local digital product, process, and sales strategy expert. Collaborate with the sales managers to train, develop and motivate the local sales team so that revenue goals are achieved. Collaborate with the sales managers to foster career growth and development of the local sales team so that a pipeline of talent for future Scripps sales management openings is ready. job.description: Are you passionate about turning data into actionable insights that drive business growth? Scripps is seeking a Senior Specialist, Media Measurement & Optimization to monitor and evaluate the performance of our paid media, on-air placement, earned media, social media, and influencer campaigns. In this role, you'll be at the center of our marketing analytics efforts, focusing on media performance metrics while acting as a liaison between Marketing and Research & Insights. This position ensures our media investments align with contractual obligations while delivering data-driven recommendations that maximize audience engagement and conversion outcomes. Review audience engagement and conversion data to understand media impact. Coordinate with Research and Insights team to validate media spend impact on business outcomes. job.title: Sr Reporter, KMVT
job.description: KMVT, The E.W. Scripps Company CBS affiliate in Twin Falls, Idaho, is seeking a Senior Reporter who is passionate about investigative journalism and meaningful storytelling. This role is perfect for a seasoned journalist ready to lead by example, mentor others, and deliver impactful stories that resonate across multiple platforms. As our Senior Reporter, you'll serve as a subject matter expert in investigative and long-form journalism while building authentic connections with our community. You'll be at the forefront of breaking news, diving deep into stories that matter, and inspiring others with your commitment to the highest journalistic standards. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Develop a network of sources throughout the community to leverage local experts. Research stories by investigating public records, personal sources, and other contacts to determine the most effective approach for a story. Use visual journalism such as graphics, photography, and videography as well as digitally distinct content. Operate camera with still and video capabilities. Serve as a lead reporter for in-depth breaking news and stay abreast of local developments. Report live on location from various news events. Fill in as morning anchor, as needed. Inspire community belonging with diversity of coverage and perspectives. Maintain current journalism capabilities to deliver high-quality reporting. Collaborate and share content, design elements, systems, workflows, and best practices. Ensure objectivity and fairness in coverage, sensitivity to community expectations and balanced content. Engage with newsroom editorial and content planning to ensure effective planning for multimedia platforms that aligns to strategy and deadlines. Participate in community events and actively engage with the community. May serve as back-up for editorial coverage. Periodically required to drive personal or company vehicle to cover various assignments. Other duties as assigned. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: BS/BA in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred Generally, 5+ years of experience in news reporting including in-depth long form reporting required Experience in community, digital and solutions-based reporting, and journalism preferred Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: High expertise in in-depth, long form reporting and application of journalistic standards Talented storyteller with a distinct and engaging on-air personality Media consumer mindset Working knowledge of multimedia journalism, e.g. news reporting, writing, web posting, still photography, online video, infographics, databases, and social media Versed in the fundamentals of news reporting, including privacy, access, ethics as well as state and federal laws regarding open meetings, open records, and access to information High standards of accuracy and fairness Outstanding editing and writing for publication Working knowledge of Associated Press style Able to use digital, video, mapping, social networking, and other technology to bolster on-air news reporting Working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook), and web publishing tools High adaptability High emotional intelligence Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY: Twin Falls, Idaho, offers a unique blend of small-town charm and outdoor adventure. Known as the gateway to the Magic Valley, Twin Falls is home to the breathtaking Shoshone Falls—often called the "Niagara of the West"—and the stunning Perrine Bridge, a popular spot for BASE jumping enthusiasts. The area boasts world-class fly fishing, hiking, and mountain biking, with easy access to Craters of the Moon National Monument and the Sawtooth Mountains. The community is welcoming and tight-knit, with a thriving downtown featuring local shops, restaurants, and cultural events. Twin Falls is also an agricultural hub, offering farm-to-table dining experiences and a strong connection to the land. With affordable living, excellent schools, and a growing economy, Twin Falls provides an exceptional quality of life for those seeking both professional fulfillment and outdoor recreation. #LI-SM2 #LI-Onsite If you are a current Scripps employee, please do not apply on this site. job.title: Customer Success Coordinator - AudioSalad (London)
job.description: AudioSalad is an industry-leading music technology platform that helps labels, distributors, artists, and rights holders manage, distribute, and optimize their digital music catalogues globally. Combining best-in-class content management, delivery, distribution, and analytics tools, AudioSalad enables its partners to reach audiences worldwide while simplifying the complexities of today's digital music landscape. The Opportunity: AudioSalad is seeking a Customer Success Coordinator to support day-to-day operational workflows across digital distribution, DSP operations, customer support, rights management, and catalog onboarding. This role will work closely with clients, DSP partners, and internal teams to help ensure high-quality content delivery, metadata accuracy, operational efficiency, and strong client support across AudioSalad’s growing distribution and supply chain business. This position is ideal for someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented, operationally minded, and excited to grow within a fast-paced music technology and digital distribution environment. What You Will Be Doing: Support day-to-day operational workflows across DSP delivery, metadata quality control, rights management, client onboarding, and catalog migrations. Handle inbound client support requests related to distribution, content delivery, platform issues, and operational troubleshooting. Review and troubleshoot metadata issues, delivery errors, ownership conflicts, and DSP platform rejections. Assist with client onboarding and catalog migration projects from external distribution partners. Monitor operational queues, support inboxes, and workflow backlogs to help ensure timely issue resolution and SLA adherence. Maintain internal SOPs, workflow documentation, and operational tracking systems. Coordinate with internal teams on high-priority operational issues and client escalations. Assist with platform compliance reviews, catalog audits, and quality control initiatives. What You'll Bring: 1–3 years of related professional experience in music distribution, digital operations, content operations, customer support, or rights management preferred. Familiarity with digital music distribution workflows, DSP ecosystems, metadata standards, and digital supply chain operations preferred. Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to effectively prioritize work in a fast-paced environment. Comfort working with spreadsheets, operational systems, support platforms, and large content catalogs. Strong written and verbal communication skills with a client-service mindset. Ability to troubleshoot operational issues independently and escalate appropriately when needed. Self-motivated, collaborative, and eager to learn within a growing and evolving business function. Professional proficiency in Spanish preferred. Why join AudioSalad: Be part of a leading music technology company supporting independent labels, distributors, artists, and rights holders around the world. Work at the intersection of music, technology, and customer success in a fast-growing global business. Collaborate with a passionate, supportive, and highly knowledgeable team. Gain exposure to digital distribution, catalogue management, metadata operations, and the evolving music streaming landscape. Help shape the future of how music is delivered and managed worldwide. This is a hybrid role that will require you to commute to our London office a minimum of three days a week.
